title: fmine-array: composite_into silently drops rows out of depth order, double-counts overlaps, and accepts a bad target length
description:
## Background
Found while rewriting `crates/fmine-array/CONTRACT.md` for BD-327.S2 (HEAD 96688ca). `ColumnarIntervalTable::composite_into` (`crates/fmine-array/src/lib.rs:262`) takes the collar depth from the first stored row (`from_blocks[0].0[0]`). Then it clamps each row's first and last bin into `0..num_bins`. `push` (`lib.rs:210`) checks only that each row is finite, that `to_m > from_m` and that density is positive. It does not check the row against the previous one.

Failure cases, found by reading the code (no test yet):
- **A row shallower than the first row is dropped.** Rows (3, 6) then (0, 3) give collar 3. The second row's bins clamp to bin 0 = [3, 5], its overlap with [3, 5] has length 0, and its mass and metal vanish. No error is returned, so conservation fails silently.
- **Overlapping rows are counted twice.**
- **A bad target length is not refused.** `target_length_m <= 0.0` returns `Ok(0)`, and a NaN target produces a single bin instead of an error.

Nothing in the workspace calls `ColumnarIntervalTable` today, so no output is wrong yet.

## Work
- `push` refuses a row whose `from_m` is less than the previous row's `to_m` (out of order or overlapping), with a typed `ArrayError` variant naming both depths. Gaps stay allowed.
- `composite_into` refuses a non-finite or non-positive `target_length_m` with a typed `ArrayError`. An empty table still returns `Ok(0)`.
- Nothing is reordered or clamped to make input fit ("refuse, never clamp").

## Acceptance criteria
- `test_push_refuses_out_of_order_and_overlapping_rows`: the (3, 6) then (0, 3) case and an overlap are both refused, and the table is unchanged.
- `test_composite_refuses_bad_target_length`: 0, a negative value, NaN and infinity are each refused.
- `test_composite_conserves_mass_across_a_gap`: rows with a gap between them conserve mass and metal.
- Mutation: removing the order check makes the first test fail.
close_reason: test:fmine_array::tests::test_push_refuses_out_of_order_and_overlapping_rows, test:fmine_array::tests::test_composite_refuses_bad_target_length, test:fmine_array::tests::test_composite_conserves_mass_across_a_gap; commit:592768b. Re-run in a fresh clone at 592768b: 5 passed. Mutants 8 of 8 killed, including the order check removed (first test fails) and the old behaviour (both refusal tests fail); the gap test also passes on the old code, as a guard. Self-verified only: no independent reviewer, and no CI run yet (not pushed).

title: BD-341 [WP-03]: Guidance track record: issuer per-site guidance FY2023–FY2026 transcribed by two readers with pages; outcomes from first-published vintages; hit rate, bias and price-conditional split, descriptive only below n_eff ≈ 35
description:
_Plan row BD-341 (WP-03). Scope in one line: Guidance track record — the issuer's per-site guidance FY2023–FY2026 transcribed by two readers and scored descriptively against first-published outcomes_

## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- Plan row's blocked-by list: BD-332, BD-047, BD-048
- plan-deps: BD-332, BD-047, BD-048
- proposed-deps: BD-332, BD-343, NEW-cited-pdf-transcriptions
- **Add BD-343.** Guidance is a range with no stated coverage. `FrozenForecast` stores only a Gaussian mean and standard deviation, and `evaluate_model` drops unresolved entries (FACT, `crates/fmine-calib/src/lib.rs:16–26, 111–160`). BD-343 adds an interval payload, cohorts and outcome vintages, so the scores must sit on it.
- **Keep BD-047 and BD-048 transitively**, through BD-343.
- **Add NEW-cited-pdf-transcriptions.** Guidance is printed in PDFs, and the repository has no PDF reader.
- blocks: BD-342 (its S2 transcription only)

Type and priority rationale: priority: 1 (the M0 transcription target is the non-forecast answer to the "nothing new" kill; scores are M1)

## Background and why it matters
All three models in the idea duel ranked an idea about the issuer's guidance first.
- **The proposal.** Claude's CC-01 scored 730 and 865 from its rivals. After the rivals steelmanned it, those scores rose to 790 and 905.
- **The premise.** A filed or posted guidance statement carries a publication date that nobody can backdate, FrankenMining included. So the issuer's own forward statements are pre-registered forecasts (INV-008), years before FrankenMining existed.
- **Why it matters for M0.** It gives finance reviewers something new that does not depend on FrankenMining's own unscored forecasting skill.

The rivals attached four conditions:
1. no recalibration at n = 3 years;
2. descriptive scores with honest intervals;
3. transcription by two readers;
4. delivery privately to the sponsor first.

§21.6 also forbids any positive calibration claim before n ≈ 35 independent outcomes. One period across about 14 sites demonstrates the protocol, not skill.

## Goal
`fmine track-record --issuer barrick --json` reports, for each site, metric and year:
- the guidance range, its page and its publication date;
- the first-published outcome and whether it landed inside the range;
- descriptive aggregates: hit rate with a Clopper–Pearson interval, the side of each miss, and bias.

Every value cites a page or a cell. FY2026 guidance is registered as the issuer's forecast family beside FrankenMining's own FY2026 forecasts (BD-067, BD-068), and both are scored on the same release.

## Current state
- **No code.** Nothing exists for guidance, and no guidance value is registered anywhere in the repository.
- **Known guidance facts.**
  - Lumwana 2026: AISC $3.40–3.75/lb (FACT, E586, AIF p.31).
  - North Mara 2026: 200–230 koz attributable, at $1,520–1,680/oz (FACT, E587 quoting AIF p.30).
- **The 2026 AIF** (dated 27 Feb 2026) was read by research pass W4 from a scratch download. It is not on disk in the corpus and not registered.
- **MD&As on disk.** The MD&As for Q1 2024 to Q2 2026 are in `corpus_of_input_docs/downloaded/mine_stats/`, but `sources.rs` registers only the 18 workbooks.
- **Documents missing from disk.** The documents that first published FY2023 and FY2024 guidance (early 2023 and early 2024) are not there (INFERENCE, from the file listing).
- **Outcomes.**
  - FY2024 and FY2025 outcomes are in the Q4 2024 and Q4 2025 Mine Stats (registered).
  - FY2023 appears only as a restated comparative in the Q4 2024 workbook, since its first publication (the Q4 2023 workbook) is not registered.

## Scope
**In:**
- source registration for the guidance documents;
- two-reader transcription;
- outcome binding;
- descriptive scores and a synthetic coverage test;
- a price-conditional split, gated per site;
- the verb.

**Out:**
- recalibration;
- site rankings when common shocks dominate;
- the guidance-at-risk nowcast (BD-342 holds the deductive version);
- any publication about the issuer.

## Design
**`GuidanceRecord`** fields:
- `issuer` and `subject`;
- `metric_key`, one of production_koz, aisc_usd_per_oz, tcc_usd_per_oz, c1_usd_per_lb, capex_usd_m;
- `basis{ownership: Attributable|Full, per_oz: Sold|Produced, credits: ByProduct|CoProduct}`;
- `period` (FY) and `value` (Range{lo,hi}, Point, AtMost or AtLeast);
- `assumptions{au_usd_oz, cu_usd_lb, …}`;
- `vintage` (Initial, Reaffirmed or Revised(n));
- `locator{doc, sha256, page, raw_token}` and `published_at`;
- `readers` (two role ids, no names).

"Equity share" guidance is attributable. It resolves against Mine Stats column C (attributable), never column B (100% basis) (E456).

**Two-reader rule.** Two independent transcriptions are diffed. A third role re-reads every disagreement, and only agreed rows enter the record.

**Outcomes** come through BD-343's cohorts:
- the default selector is the first-published vintage;
- restated values are scored separately;
- FY2023 is labelled `resolved_on_comparative_vintage`;
- divested or NOT_PUBLISHED members stay in the denominator as unresolved. Examples: Hemlo, sold 26 Nov 2025; Tongon, sold 1 Dec 2025 (E487); Loulo-Gounkoto 2025 (E818).

**Scores** are descriptive only.
- For a range [L, U], let m = (L + U)/2, h = (U − L)/2 and z = (y − m)/h.
- Report the hit rate k/n with a Clopper–Pearson interval, the share above the midpoint, and mean z with its interval.
- Also report n_eff, set to the number of years when the year effect dominates.
- Synthetic example: guidance [100, 120] and outcome 125 give z = +1.5, a miss on the high side.

**Price-conditional split** (HYPOTHESIS, gated per site). For an ad valorem royalty, the price-driven part of an AISC miss is r·(1 − P_assumed/P_realized).
- It is applied only where a per-site regression over the registered quarters supports royalty-per-ounce ∝ price. Otherwise the miss stays unsplit.
- The unconditional and conditional scores are always shown side by side.

**Delivery and disclosure.**
- The report goes privately to the sponsor first. FrankenMining publishes nothing about the issuer.
- Any external use of the report goes to counsel first, during the pre-release quiet period (§37.3).
- Every output is labelled "from public filings; no affiliation implied".

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Every guidance and outcome value reproduces its cited page or cell, with two-reader agreement on 100% of entered rows.
2. Over at least 200 synthetic replicates with known coverage and bias, the 90% intervals for hit rate and bias cover the truth 85–95% of the time.
3. **Week-1 data gate.** Count the resolved years × sites with citations. If fewer than 3 × 10, ship single-site guidance cards for North Mara and Lumwana instead, and record that the gate fired.
4. FY2026 guidance is registered with its `published_at` before any FY2026 outcome is available.
5. Below n_eff ≈ 35, no output carries a calibration verdict.

## Tests
- **Parity.** Transcription fixtures carry their capture records and are never regenerated from the candidate.
- **Known answers.** A generator draws ranges with known c and μ and with year and site effects. The coverage criterion above applies.
- **Properties.**
  - Scores are invariant under exact unit changes.
  - The price split is the identity when P_realized = P_assumed.
  - An attributable guidance row is never scored against a 100% outcome (mutation test).
- **No hindsight.**
  - A guidance vintage is admissible only if `published_at` precedes the outcome's availability time (G-TIME-2).
  - The forecast horizon is part of the segment.
- **Denominator.** Withholding any outcome leaves n unchanged (BD-343 property).

## Risks, kill criteria and fallbacks
- **The data gate fires.** Fall back to single-site cards.
- **Management reads the report as an attack.** Deliver privately and show the controllable score.
- **Common shocks dominate.** Refuse site rankings with FMINE-REF-104 (non-identifiable) and report the year-shock finding only.
- **Basis traps:** attributable against 100%, $/lb for Lumwana, regions under the versioned region map (E461), copper in kt (E463).
- **Never:**
  - claim "beats guidance" without an e-value;
  - treat implied figures as the issuer's own;
  - use non-public information.

## Subtasks
- **S1. Register guidance source documents.**
  - Contents: the AIFs and the full-year MD&As or releases that carry FY2023–FY2026 guidance, with URL, bytes, sha256 and `published_at`.
  - Also produce the week-1 data-gate count.
  - Acceptance: every needed document is either registered or listed as missing with its expected URL.
  - Deps: NEW-cited-pdf-transcriptions.
- **S2. Two-reader transcription, FY2023–FY2026.**
  - Covers production, TCC or C1, AISC and capex for every gold and copper site.
  - Acceptance: criterion 1.
  - Deps: S1.
- **S3. Outcome binding.**
  - Contents: the FY blocks of the Q4 workbooks, BD-332 keys, the region map and unit rules, comparative-vintage labelling.
  - Deps: BD-332, S2.
- **S4. Descriptive scores**, with the synthetic generator and the coverage test.
  - Deps: BD-343, S3.
- **S5. Price-conditional split**, with the per-site proportionality test.
  - Deps: S4.
- **S6. `fmine track-record` verb.**
  - Contents: the §30.1 envelope, the verb's registration in `verbs.toml`, the `no_claim` line and the no-affiliation label.
  - Deps: S4.

## References
- Plan: §21.6 "FY2026 forecast record" (lines 4594–4626); §37.3 M0 TARGET bullet and M1 (lines 7612–7662); K.5 row 4 (line 9392); bead row at line 8014.
- Duel: CC-01 (`planning/duel/WIZARD_IDEAS_CC.md` §2); steelman results in `DUELING_WIZARDS_REPORT.md`.
- Evidence: E456, E461, E463, E487, E586, E587, E818.
- Code: `crates/fmine-calib/src/lib.rs`.

## E2E test script and logging
- **E2E.** S6's verb `fmine track-record --issuer synthetic --json` runs on the generator's known-answer issuer. The script asserts the recovered coverage and bias inside their stated tolerance, and that withholding one outcome leaves `n_members` unchanged. When the transcriptions exist, the same verb runs `--issuer barrick` and its output is compared with the two-reader transcription digests.
- **Logging.** One line per scored row: site, year, metric, guidance range with its document locator, outcome with its Claim id, basis (attributable or 100%), price split, score. One cohort line: `n_members`, `n_resolved`, `n_overdue`, `n_withheld`. A row refused on basis or hindsight logs its refusal code and the two timestamps compared.

title: BD-341.S1 [WP-03]: Register guidance source documents
description:
## Context
Subtask S1 of BD-341: "BD-341 [WP-03]: Guidance track record: issuer per-site guidance FY2023–FY2026 transcribed by two readers with pages; outcomes from first-published vintages; hit rate, bias and price-conditional split, descriptive only below n_eff ≈ 35". The parent bead carries the full background, current state, design, tests and risks; read it first (`br show <parent>`; the parent link is set).

**Parent goal.** `fmine track-record --issuer barrick --json` reports, for each site, metric and year:
- the guidance range, its page and its publication date;
- the first-published outcome and whether it landed inside the range;
- descriptive aggregates: hit rate with a Clopper–Pearson interval, the side of each miss, and bias.

Every value cites a page or a cell. FY2026 guidance is registered as the issuer's forecast family beside FrankenMining's own FY2026 forecasts (BD-067, BD-068), and both are scored on the same release.

## Work
REVIEW: the gate rule "fewer than 3 × 10" is ambiguous: at least 30 resolved site-years in total, or at least 10 sites resolved in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025. Report both counts. The owner picks the rule before the count is run.

This subtask registers documents and counts. It transcribes nothing; S2 does that.

**Builds on NEW-cited-pdf-transcriptions.** That bead adds `SourceKind::{MdA, Aif, InvestorDeck, PartnerFiling}`, plus `published_at` and `published_at_basis`, to `RegisteredSource` (`crates/fmine-public/src/sources.rs:35`). It also adds the load-time digest check (FMINE-REF-502, as in `load_registered_sources`, `crates/fmine-public/src/lib.rs:126`). Use that format only. Never invent a second registry.

**Files.** `crates/fmine-public/src/sources.rs`:
- `BARRICK_GUIDANCE_SOURCES`: one `RegisteredSource` per document that first publishes, reaffirms or revises FY2023–FY2026 per-site guidance;
- `BARRICK_GUIDANCE_MISSING: &[MissingSource]` (DESIGN), with fields `{expected_file, kind, guidance_years, expected_url, url_basis, why_needed}`.

**Known candidates (FACT unless marked):**
- **2025 AIF**, dated 27 Feb 2026. It carries Lumwana 2026 AISC (p.31, E586) and North Mara 2026 production and AISC (p.30, E587).
  - It is not on disk. W4 recorded only the sha256 prefix `d8bc75c700aa8892`.
  - Download it into `corpus_of_input_docs/downloaded/` and register the full digest.
  - If the digest differs from W4's, register it as a new vintage.
- **Q4 MD&As on disk:**
  - `Barrick_Q4_2024_MD-A.pdf`: 2,338,137 bytes, sha256 `43dcfca7…`, 147 pages;
  - `Barrick_Q4_2025_MD-A.pdf`: 2,286,439 bytes, sha256 `63b3af0b…`, 140 pages.

  These figures are from W1 §2.2. Whether these MD&As print per-site next-year guidance is OPEN until a reader checks the pages.
- **Q1–Q3 MD&As, 2024–2026** (on disk). Register each one only if it carries a reaffirmed or revised guidance statement (S2's `vintage`).
- **FY2023 and FY2024 sources.** The documents that first published this guidance (early 2023 and early 2024) are not on disk (INFERENCE). Fetch and register them, or list them as missing with an expected URL.

**`published_at`.** It is FACT only when the date is cited from the document or its release. Otherwise it is INFERENCE, with its basis stated.

**Week-1 data gate.** Add `guidance_gate(census: &[GuidanceCensusRow]) -> GuidanceGate{site_years_resolved, sites_all_three_years, fired_total_rule, fired_grid_rule}`.
- One reader's page survey supplies the census rows `(site, fy, metric, doc, page)`.
- A site-year counts only if two things hold: a registered guidance page exists, and a registered outcome cell exists.
- FY2026 never counts, because its outcomes arrive in Feb 2027.
- If the gate fires, record it in the close reason. S6 then ships single-site cards for North Mara and Lumwana.

**Handover to S2:** the registered documents, the missing list and the census.

**Never:**
- commit PDF bytes (a `*.pdf` path rule applies in CI);
- register a document whose digest was not computed from bytes on disk;
- take a value or a date from `corpus_of_input_docs/markdown_extractions/` without re-reading the PDF page.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every document needed for FY2023–FY2026 per-site guidance is in one of two places:
  - a registered row with file, kind, URL, url_basis, bytes, sha256, `published_at` and `published_at_basis`;
  - a `MissingSource` row with its expected URL and reason.
- The 2025 AIF is registered with a full sha256. Either its first 16 hex digits equal `d8bc75c700aa8892` (W4), or the difference is recorded as a new vintage.
- A missing or altered registered PDF refuses with FMINE-REF-502 and names the file.
- The gate counts are reported under both rules, and the close reason records whether the gate fired.
- No `*.pdf` file is tracked by git.

## Tests and logging
**Unit tests:**
- `test_guidance_registry_is_well_formed`: names are unique; sha256 is 64 lowercase hex characters; bytes > 0; `published_at` parses as `fmine_time::CivilDate`; the basis is FACT or INFERENCE.
- `test_missing_guidance_sources_carry_expected_url`.
- `test_guidance_gate_total_rule_boundary`: synthetic census; 29 site-years fire the gate and 30 do not.
- `test_guidance_gate_grid_rule_boundary`: 9 sites resolved in all three years fire the gate; 10 do not.
- `test_guidance_gate_never_counts_fy2026`.

**Negative control:**
- `test_altered_guidance_pdf_refuses_naming_file`: a one-byte change to a temp copy under `target/` refuses with FMINE-REF-502, naming the file.

**Ignored real-file test.** `test_guidance_sources_match_registered_digests` needs the gitignored corpus. It runs in BD-339's CI job, whose fetch list gains these URLs.
- Per file: `{"event":"guidance_source","file","kind","bytes","sha256","published_at","published_at_basis","status"}`, where `status` is ok, missing or altered.
- Summary: `{"event":"guidance_sources_summary","registered","present","missing","altered","site_years_resolved","sites_all_three_years","fired_total_rule","fired_grid_rule"}`.

## Close rule
Close only with this subtask's own evidence, as typed references: `test:<crate>::<path>::<fn>`, `commit:<sha7>`, `record:<path>`, `ci:<run-id>@<sha7>` or an E id. Never a shared or generic reason (K.2 finding 4).

title: BD-341.S2 [WP-03]: Two-reader transcription, FY2023–FY2026
description:
## Context
Subtask S2 of BD-341: "BD-341 [WP-03]: Guidance track record: issuer per-site guidance FY2023–FY2026 transcribed by two readers with pages; outcomes from first-published vintages; hit rate, bias and price-conditional split, descriptive only below n_eff ≈ 35". - the guidance range, its page and its publication date;

Every value cites a page or a cell. FY2026 guidance is registered as the issuer's forecast family beside FrankenMining's own FY2026 forecasts (BD-067, BD-068), and both are scored on the same release.

## Work
REVIEW: the dossier's `metric_key` list (production_koz, aisc_usd_per_oz, tcc_usd_per_oz, c1_usd_per_lb, capex_usd_m) has no key for copper AISC in $/lb or copper production in kt. So the Lumwana 2026 AISC row ($3.40–3.75/lb, E586) cannot be entered. Add `aisc_usd_per_lb` and `production_kt` (copper is printed in kt, E463).

**Files.** New module `crates/fmine-public/src/guidance.rs` (`pub mod guidance;` in `lib.rs`).

**`GuidanceRecord`** follows the dossier:
- `issuer` and `subject`, where the subject must be in `BARRICK_SUBJECTS` (`sources.rs:267`) or an S1-registered copper site;
- `metric_key`;
- `basis{ownership: Attributable|Full, per_oz: Sold|Produced, credits: ByProduct|CoProduct}`;
- `period` (FY) and `value` (`Range{lo,hi} | Point | AtMost | AtLeast`), held as exact rationals with a `step` taken from the printed digits;
- `assumptions{au_usd_oz, cu_usd_lb, …}`, each one itself a transcribed value with its page;
- `vintage` (`Initial | Reaffirmed | Revised(n)`);
- `locator{doc, sha256, page, raw_token}` and `published_at`;
- `readers`: two role ids, never names.

**Rows.** The rows are NEW-cited-pdf-transcriptions' `TranscribedValue`s.
- Reader A and reader B enter them as two independent Rust constant arrays (`BARRICK_GUIDANCE_ROWS_A` and `_B`).

- Disagreements go to a third role for re-reading. They are never auto-resolved.

**Basis rule.** "Equity share" guidance is `Attributable` and resolves against Mine Stats column C (E456).

**Minimum rows.** These are also the single-site fallback cards if S1's gate fires.
- Lumwana FY2026 AISC: `Range[3.40, 3.75]` $/lb, step 0.01 (E586, AIF p.31).
- North Mara FY2026 production: `Range[200, 230]` koz attributable, raw token "200 - 230" (E587, AIF p.30).
- North Mara FY2026 AISC: `Range[1,520, 1,680]` $/oz (E587).

**Scope.** Production, TCC or C1, AISC and capex, for every gold and copper site in S1's registered documents, FY2023–FY2026. A cell with no row carries a named reason: not guided, document missing, or site divested.

**Registering the FY2026 issuer family (criterion 4).**
- Hand the FY2026 rows to BD-343 as `ForecastPayload::Interval{lo, hi, nominal: None}` under a separate model key, beside BD-067 and BD-068.
- The record time is the actual time of FrankenMining's registration, before Q4 2026 outcomes exist.
- Never set the record time to `published_at`: that would backdate FrankenMining's own act.

**Historical years (FY2023–FY2025).** Their outcomes are already public, so they must not go through `ForecastLedger::register` (`crates/fmine-calib/src/lib.rs:42`). They enter BD-343 cohorts as issuer-published forecasts. Their admissibility rests on the cited `published_at` preceding the outcome's availability (G-TIME-2).

**Handover to S3:** the agreed rows.

**Never:**
- regenerate the fixtures from the candidate;
- transcribe from markdown mirrors;
- transcribe any person's name;
- treat implied figures as the issuer's own.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Criterion 1.** Every entered row reproduces its cited page token: `raw_token`, page and labels. Two-reader agreement holds on 100% of entered rows.
- The disagreement list is empty, or every item carries a third-reader resolution record.

  - "200 - 230" gives [200, 230] with step 1;

  - "(708)" gives −708.

title: BD-341.S3 [WP-03]: Outcome binding
description:
## Context
Subtask S3 of BD-341: "BD-341 [WP-03]: Guidance track record: issuer per-site guidance FY2023–FY2026 transcribed by two readers with pages; outcomes from first-published vintages; hit rate, bias and price-conditional split, descriptive only below n_eff ≈ 35". The parent bead carries the full background, current state, design, tests and risks; read it first (`br show <parent>`; the parent link is set).

**Parent goal.** `fmine track-record --issuer barrick --json` reports, for each site, metric and year:
- the guidance range, its page and its publication date;
- the first-published outcome and whether it landed inside the range;
- descriptive aggregates: hit rate with a Clopper–Pearson interval, the side of each miss, and bias.

Every value cites a page or a cell. FY2026 guidance is registered as the issuer's forecast family beside FrankenMining's own FY2026 forecasts (BD-067, BD-068), and both are scored on the same release.

## Work
**Goal.** Bind each agreed guidance row from S2 to its first-published FY outcome, keyed with BD-332's `PublicKey`. Hand the bound outcomes to BD-343 as `OutcomeEvent`s.

**Files.** `crates/fmine-public/src/guidance.rs`:
- `bind_outcome(rec: &GuidanceRecord, sources: &[LoadedSource], keys: &PublicKeyIndex) -> OutcomeBinding`;
- `OutcomeBinding` is either `Resolved{claim, vintage: FirstPublished | Comparative, at, sha256}` or `Unresolved{reason: NotPublished | Divested | Withheld | DefinitionChanged | NoCell}`.

**Where outcomes come from (FACT, registered):**
- **FY2024:** the FY blocks of `Barrick_Q4_2024_Mine_Stats.xlsx` (sha256 `f5e7db7c…`).
- **FY2025:** `Barrick_Q4_2025_Mine_Stats.xlsx` (`94f6692a…`).
- **Per-site FY AISC:** where the Mine Stats block lacks it, use the annual sheet of the Q4 AISC workbook (for example sheet `2025`, E691).
- **FY2023:** it exists only as a restated comparative in the Q4 2024 workbook. Its first publication (the Q4 2023 workbook) is not registered. Every FY2023 binding is labelled `resolved_on_comparative_vintage` and scored separately in S4.

**Rules:**
- **Ownership.** `Attributable` guidance binds only to Mine Stats column C, never to column B (100% basis) (E456). A cross-basis bind refuses with FMINE-REF-105 (basis mismatch).
- **Selector.** First-published by default. A later restatement is a separate `Restated` event, never an overwrite. That follows BD-343's E474 pattern: 1,479 first published, later shown as 1,474.
- **Units.**
  - Copper quantities are kt. Some 2024 Minestats4 labels say "millions of pounds" over kt values (E463); take the unit from the BD-332 unit registry, never from the label.
  - Lumwana costs are in $/lb.
  - Units never convert implicitly.
- **Regions.** Score sites only. A region-level row binds only under the region-map version of its vintage: Pueblo Viejo moves to North America from Q4 2025 and comparatives are restated (E461).
- **Denominator.** Divested, withheld or not-published members stay in the denominator as `Unresolved` (BD-343 `Missing{…}`):
  - Hemlo, sold 26 Nov 2025;
  - Tongon, sold 1 Dec 2025 (E487);
  - Loulo-Gounkoto 2025 (E818).
- **Loulo-Gounkoto FY2025 is OPEN.** FY2025 YTD cells exist: `Q4_2025:YTD!E16` 4,271 and `G16` 1,603, with FY sold equal to Q4 sold, 91 (W1-DR-07). Whether they form a full-year outcome is decided by BD-332's subject-status registry, which marks the site withheld for 2025Q1–Q3. The default is `Unresolved(DefinitionChanged)`.
- **Two families, two bases.** FrankenMining's own FY2026 forecasts target the 100% basis (§21.6, column B), while the issuer's guidance family is attributable. Both are scored on the same release, each on its own basis, and never cross-scored.

**Builds on:** BD-332 (keys and subject status) and S2 (rows).
**Hands over:** `OutcomeEvent::Published{value, vintage, locator, sha256}` or `Missing{reason}` per member, to S4 through BD-343 cohorts.

**Never:**
- pick the latest vintage silently;
- drop an unresolved member;
- treat a comparative vintage as first-published;
- default an unprinted ownership basis to 100%.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every `Resolved` outcome reproduces its cell, `<file>:<Sheet>!<Cell>`, and that file's registered sha256 (criterion 1, outcome side).
- Mutation: binding an attributable row to a column-B cell is refused, never scored.
- All FY2023 bindings carry `resolved_on_comparative_vintage`.
- Hemlo and Tongon FY2025 and Loulo-Gounkoto 2025 are `Unresolved` with their reasons. `n_members` is unchanged.
- No region row binds across region-map versions.

## Tests and logging
**Unit tests on synthetic workbooks** (built with `fmine_io::xlsx::build_minimal_xlsx`, in the style of `synthetic.rs`):
- `test_attributable_row_never_binds_to_100pct_column` (mutation test; E456);
- `test_fy2023_outcome_labelled_comparative_vintage`;
- `test_divested_members_stay_in_denominator` (Hemlo, Tongon, Loulo-Gounkoto);
- `test_first_published_selector_ignores_later_restatement` (synthetic 1,479 → 1,474);
- `test_copper_quantity_unit_from_registry_not_label` (E463);
- `test_region_binding_respects_map_version` (E461);
- `test_unprinted_basis_refuses` (negative control).

**Ignored real-file test.** `test_guidance_outcomes_bind_to_q4_workbooks` runs in BD-339's CI job.
- Per binding: `{"event":"guidance_outcome","site","metric","fy","vintage","at","sha256","token","state","reason"}`, where `state` is resolved or unresolved.
- Summary: `{"event":"guidance_outcomes_summary","members","resolved_first_published","resolved_comparative","unresolved_by_reason"}`.

## Close rule
Close only with this subtask's own evidence, as typed references: `test:<crate>::<path>::<fn>`, `commit:<sha7>`, `record:<path>`, `ci:<run-id>@<sha7>` or an E id. Never a shared or generic reason (K.2 finding 4).

- Mutation: binding an attributable row to a column-B cell is refused, never scored.

- Hemlo and Tongon FY2025 and Loulo-Gounkoto 2025 are `Unresolved` with their reasons. `n_members` is unchanged.
- No region row binds across region-map versions.

title: BD-341.S4 [WP-03]: Descriptive scores
description:
## Context
Subtask S4 of BD-341: "BD-341 [WP-03]: Guidance track record: issuer per-site guidance FY2023–FY2026 transcribed by two readers with pages; outcomes from first-published vintages; hit rate, bias and price-conditional split, descriptive only below n_eff ≈ 35". The parent bead carries the full background, current state, design, tests and risks; read it first (`br show <parent>`; the parent link is set).

**Parent goal.** `fmine track-record --issuer barrick --json` reports, for each site, metric and year:
- the guidance range, its page and its publication date;
- the first-published outcome and whether it landed inside the range;
- descriptive aggregates: hit rate with a Clopper–Pearson interval, the side of each miss, and bias.

Every value cites a page or a cell. FY2026 guidance is registered as the issuer's forecast family beside FrankenMining's own FY2026 forecasts (BD-067, BD-068), and both are scored on the same release.

## Work
**Goal.** Descriptive scores over BD-343 assessments: no recalibration, no ranking, no verdict.

**Files.** New module `crates/fmine-calib/src/guidance_scores.rs`.

**Builds on.** BD-343's `Assessment` (selector `FirstPublished`; restated values scored separately) and S3's bindings.

**Do not use `ForecastLedger::evaluate_model`** (`crates/fmine-calib/src/lib.rs:111`). It drops unresolved entries and sets `Calibrated`, `Biased` or `Overconfident` at any n ≥ 1.

**Per member.** `score_range(lo, hi, y) -> RangeScore{m, h, z, side: Below|Inside|Above, boundary: bool}`:
- m = (L + U)/2, h = (U − L)/2, z = (y − m)/h, in exact rationals (BD-340 `Rat`, or `ExactQty` plus BD-340's add and sub).
- Synthetic known answer: [100, 120] and y = 125 give z = +3/2, side Above.
- `boundary` marks an outcome whose printed rounding interval straddles L or U. It is reported, never hidden (DESIGN).
- `Point`, `AtMost` and `AtLeast` rows enter the hit rate only. Their z is undefined and is never computed.

**Aggregates per (metric, FY, vintage selector):**
- **Hit rate.** k/n with a two-sided 90% Clopper–Pearson interval.
  - Compute it by bisection on the exact binomial tail polynomial: no std transcendentals (NEW-det-portable-kernels).
  - Use NEW-irr-refuses' refusing root finder, so non-convergence refuses.
- **Share above the midpoint**, and the side of each miss.
- **Mean z** with an interval.
- **n_eff**, set to the number of years when the year effect dominates.
- **BD-343's whole-cohort bound** [k/n, (k + n_unresolved)/n]. Divested members stay in n.

**OPEN, decided by the coverage test.** Owner: the S4 implementer, signed off by the lead.
- The bias-interval method:
  - (a) a t-interval on per-year mean z, using a registered table of t quantiles;
  - (b) a Philox cluster bootstrap by year.
- The "year effect dominates" rule that sets n_eff.

**Synthetic generator.** `GuidanceWorld{sites, years, coverage c, bias μ, year_sd, site_sd, seed}`.
- It draws ranges with known c and μ, using `fmine_core::rand::PhiloxStream` (`rand.rs:78`) keyed by `RngKey`.
- It lives in test code in fmine-calib and is labelled synthetic. It moves to fmine-gen when BD-127 lands.
- Scenarios: no effects, year-dominant, and site-dominant.

**Flags.** Below n_eff ≈ 35 (§21.6) the flag is `Descriptive` or `Unscored`, never `Calibrated` (criterion 5).

**Common shocks.** When the year effect dominates, site rankings refuse with FMINE-REF-104 (non-identifiable). Today `REFUSAL_CATALOG` maps 104 to a density message (`crates/fmine-evidence/src/lib.rs:90`); BD-328 fixes that.

**Hands over:** score records to S5 (conditional split) and S6 (rendering).

**Never:**
- recalibrate;
- claim "beats guidance" without an e-value;
- emit a calibration verdict.

## Acceptance Criteria
- z known answer: [100, 120] with y = 125 gives exactly 3/2, a miss on the high side.
- **Criterion 2.** Run at least 200 replicates for each of the three scenarios. The 90% intervals for hit rate and bias cover the truth in 85–95% of replicates. The coverage and replicate count are reported per scenario.
- Scores are invariant under exact unit changes.
- Withholding any outcome leaves n unchanged.
- **Criterion 5.** No output below n_eff ≈ 35 carries a calibration verdict.

## Tests and logging
**Known answers and units:**
- `test_range_score_known_answer_z_three_halves`.
- `test_clopper_pearson_closed_form_edges`: k = 0, n = 10 gives upper 1 − 0.05^(1/10) ≈ 0.258866; k = n = 10 gives lower ≈ 0.741134 (INFERENCE, closed form). The test checks with `fmine_core::det` exp and ln.
- `test_clopper_pearson_refuses_on_nonconvergence`.
- `test_point_and_bound_rows_have_no_z`.

**Properties:**
- `test_scores_invariant_under_exact_unit_change`: oz ↔ g at 31.1034768.
- `test_withholding_outcome_keeps_n`.
- `test_no_calibration_verdict_below_neff_35`.

**Refusal:**
- `test_year_dominant_world_refuses_site_ranking`.

**Coverage run (not ignored):**
- `test_synthetic_coverage_200_replicates_per_scenario`.

**Mutation check:**
- `test_wald_interval_mutation_fails_coverage`: swapping in a Wald interval gives zero width at k = n and fails the coverage test.

**Log lines:**
- Per scenario: `{"event":"guidance_coverage","scenario","replicates","true_c","true_mu","hit_cover","bias_cover","neff_rule"}`.
- Summary: `{"event":"guidance_coverage_summary","scenarios","all_within_85_95"}`.

## Close rule
Close only with this subtask's own evidence, as typed references: `test:<crate>::<path>::<fn>`, `commit:<sha7>`, `record:<path>`, `ci:<run-id>@<sha7>` or an E id. Never a shared or generic reason (K.2 finding 4).
acceptance_criteria:
- z known answer: [100, 120] with y = 125 gives exactly 3/2, a miss on the high side.
- **Criterion 2.** Run at least 200 replicates for each of the three scenarios. The 90% intervals for hit rate and bias cover the truth in 85–95% of replicates. The coverage and replicate count are reported per scenario.
- Scores are invariant under exact unit changes.
- Withholding any outcome leaves n unchanged.
- **Criterion 5.** No output below n_eff ≈ 35 carries a calibration verdict.
notes: FACT: canonical guidance scores and site-history summary Claims now preserve source ancestry, evidence, knowledge state, confidentiality, UU terms and certified rational reference bounds through the retrospective CLI. Existing Annual GDA1-v2 identities remain unchanged; SiteHistory uses an explicit support and rejects duplicate years/mixed sites or bases. Evidence: test:fmine-calib::guidance_scores::claims::tests::site_history_claim_preserves_years_unresolved_members_and_exact_bounds; test:fmine-calib::guidance_scores::claims::tests::site_history_refuses_duplicate_years_and_mixed_site_or_basis; test:fmine-calib::guidance_scores::claims::tests::assumed_unknown_arithmetic_preserves_state_and_never_accepts_negative_states. title: BD-341.S5 [WP-03]: Price-conditional split
description:
## Context
Subtask S5 of BD-341: "BD-341 [WP-03]: Guidance track record: issuer per-site guidance FY2023–FY2026 transcribed by two readers with pages; outcomes from first-published vintages; hit rate, bias and price-conditional split, descriptive only below n_eff ≈ 35". The parent bead carries the full background, current state, design, tests and risks; read it first (`br show <parent>`; the parent link is set).

**Parent goal.** `fmine track-record --issuer barrick --json` reports, for each site, metric and year:
- the guidance range, its page and its publication date;
- the first-published outcome and whether it landed inside the range;
- descriptive aggregates: hit rate with a Clopper–Pearson interval, the side of each miss, and bias.

Every value cites a page or a cell. FY2026 guidance is registered as the issuer's forecast family beside FrankenMining's own FY2026 forecasts (BD-067, BD-068), and both are scored on the same release.

## Work
**Status: HYPOTHESIS, gated per site.** The split always sits beside the unconditional score and never replaces it.

**Files:**
- `crates/fmine-public/src/guidance.rs`, which binds the royalty and price inputs as cited Claims;
- `crates/fmine-calib/src/guidance_scores.rs`, which adds a conditional score beside S4's.

**Rule (from the dossier).** For an ad valorem royalty, the price-driven part of an AISC miss is
p = r·(1 − P_assumed/P_realized).

Its inputs:
- **r: realised royalty per ounce for the site.** Mine Stats prints it per site, under "Costs per ounce ($/oz)" as "Royalties". The key is `royalties_usd_per_oz` (`planning/corpus/C1_barrick_public_stats.md:137`).
- **P_assumed: the guidance price assumption.** S2 transcribes it in `assumptions.au_usd_oz` or `cu_usd_lb`, with its page.
- **P_realized: the realised price for the same period.**
  - Whether a per-site realised price is printed is OPEN; the first reader of the MD&A decides.
  - If none is printed, use the company realised price from the MD&A, transcribed through NEW-cited-pdf-transcriptions, and say so.

**Conditional score.** z_c = (y − p − m)/h, beside S4's z. Both always appear side by side.

**Scope.** The split applies only to AISC: gold AISC, and copper AISC, which includes royalties. It never applies to C1, which excludes royalties (C1 notes, A8), or to TCC (DESIGN).

**Per-site proportionality gate (DESIGN).** `royalty_proportional(site, quarters) -> Gate{beta_interval} | NotSupported{witness_quarters}`.
- Use the registered quarters, Q1 2024–Q2 2026.
- Test exact interval feasibility, in BD-340's style: is there a β such that every printed royalty (± half its step) equals β times the printed realised price (± half its step)?
- The feasible set is ∩_q [(r_q − ½)/(P_q + ½s), (r_q + ½)/(P_q − ½s)].
- An empty intersection refutes proportionality, and the miss stays unsplit for that site. Report the two quarters that witness the conflict.
- Whether a tolerance-based regression may replace the exact test is OPEN for the owner. Default: exact.

**Worked synthetic (labelled).** r = $100/oz, P_assumed = $1,500 and P_realized = $2,000 give p = 100·(1 − 3/4) = $25/oz.

**Context.** E607 says FY2025 company gold AISC of $1,637/oz was "slightly above guidance due to higher royalites driven by the higher realized gold price". That is a company statement, not a per-site split. Never cite it as a site's split.

**Builds on:** S4's `RangeScore`, and S2's `assumptions`.
**Hands over:** `ConditionalScore{p, z_c, gate}` to S6.

**Never:**
- split a site whose gate fails;
- infer P_assumed when guidance prints none (the row is unsplit, reason "no stated price assumption");
- present the conditional score alone;
- call the remainder "controllable" without the gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The split is the identity when P_realized = P_assumed: p = 0, so z_c = z.
- The synthetic example gives p = 25 exactly.
- Every site carries a gate result:
  - `Gate{beta_interval}` with its quarters cited; or
  - `NotSupported` with the conflicting quarters; or
  - unsplit with a reason.
- No output carries z_c without z.
- Every input (r, P_assumed, P_realized) cites a cell or a page and its sha256.

## Tests and logging
**Known answers:**
- `test_price_split_identity_when_prices_equal` (property).
- `test_price_split_synthetic_known_answer_25`.

**Gate:**
- `test_proportionality_gate_feasible_beta_interval`: synthetic quarters that are exactly proportional within rounding.
- `test_proportionality_gate_refuted_names_witness_quarters` (negative control).

**Refusal and scope:**
- `test_no_price_assumption_leaves_miss_unsplit`.
- `test_split_never_applied_to_c1_or_tcc`.

**Mutation check:**
- `test_conditional_score_never_rendered_alone`: removing z from the record fails validation.

**Ignored real-file test.** `test_royalty_proportionality_gate_real_quarters` runs in BD-339's CI job.
- Per site: `{"event":"price_split_gate","site","quarters","beta_lo","beta_hi","state","witness"}`, where `state` is supported, not_supported or no_assumption.
- Summary: `{"event":"price_split_summary","sites","supported","not_supported","no_assumption"}`.

## Close rule
Close only with this subtask's own evidence, as typed references: `test:<crate>::<path>::<fn>`, `commit:<sha7>`, `record:<path>`, `ci:<run-id>@<sha7>` or an E id. Never a shared or generic reason (K.2 finding 4).
acceptance_criteria:
- The split is the identity when P_realized = P_assumed: p = 0, so z_c = z.

title: BD-341.S6 [WP-03]: `fmine track-record` verb
description:
## Context
Subtask S6 of BD-341: "BD-341 [WP-03]: Guidance track record: issuer per-site guidance FY2023–FY2026 transcribed by two readers with pages; outcomes from first-published vintages; hit rate, bias and price-conditional split, descriptive only below n_eff ≈ 35". The parent bead carries the full background, current state, design, tests and risks; read it first (`br show <parent>`; the parent link is set).

**Parent goal.** `fmine track-record --issuer barrick --json` reports, for each site, metric and year:
- the guidance range, its page and its publication date;
- the first-published outcome and whether it landed inside the range;
- descriptive aggregates: hit rate with a Clopper–Pearson interval, the side of each miss, and bias.

Every value cites a page or a cell. FY2026 guidance is registered as the issuer's forecast family beside FrankenMining's own FY2026 forecasts (BD-067, BD-068), and both are scored on the same release.

## Work
**Goal.** `fmine track-record --issuer barrick [--site <subject>] [--json]` renders S2–S5 as the §30.1 envelope.

**Files and changes:**
- **`crates/fmine-cli/src/lib.rs`:**
  - add `CliCommand::TrackRecord{issuer, site: Option<String>}` to the enum at line 19;
  - parse it in `parse_args` (line 118), where an unknown issuer is a usage error with exit 2;
  - dispatch it in `execute_command` (line 211);
  - add `"track-record --issuer <issuer>"` to the robot-docs verb list (line 284).
- **`registries/verbs.toml`:** `[[verb]] path = "track-record"`, `subsystem = "Plumb"`, `mutates_authority = false`.
- **`crates/fmine-public/src/guidance.rs`:** `run_track_record(profile, root) -> Result<TrackRecordReport, Refusal>`.
  - It loads the registered workbooks (`load_registered_sources`, `lib.rs:126`) and the registered PDFs.
  - A missing or altered file refuses with FMINE-REF-502, naming the file (exit 8).

**Envelope (§30.1).** One event per line:
- one `track_record.row` event per (site, metric, FY, vintage);
- one `track_record.summary` event per (metric, FY, selector);
- a final `track_record.run`.

Each event carries:
- `flags`: all four false, with no setter (INV-002);
- `certificate`: the blake3 digest of the canonical rows (`Encoder` frame, rows sorted);
- `warnings` and `next_actions`.

If BD-329's envelope rewrite has not landed, use today's `Envelope` (`lib.rs:34`), with the events in `payload`.

**Citations (BD-329 shapes).**
- Guidance values are `extracted`, with `at` = `<doc>:p<page>:<row>/<col>` and the sha256.
- Outcomes are `extracted` cells.
- z, hit rate and the Clopper–Pearson bounds are `derived`, with rule ids such as `guidance.z`, `guidance.hit_rate.cp90` and `guidance.price_split`.
- Counts use the `count` shape.

**Required text.** Every output carries "from public filings; no affiliation implied". The `no_claim` text holds no digits, because BD-329 rule (e) rejects digits in prose. Proposed wording: "Describes how the issuer's published per-site guidance compared with its first-published outcomes. Descriptive only: no calibration verdict below the registered minimum effective sample size, no site ranking, no forecast."

**Data gate.** If S1's gate fired, the verb renders only the North Mara and Lumwana single-site cards (E586, E587), with `gate_fired: true` and the counts.

**Delivery.** The output stays on stdout, with no network and no files written. It goes privately to the sponsor first. External use goes to counsel during the pre-release quiet period (§37.3).

**Builds on:** S4, plus S5 when that has landed. The conditional score is shown only beside the unconditional one.

**Never print:**
- a calibration verdict;
- "beats guidance";
- a site ranking (a request for one refuses with FMINE-REF-104);
- any implied figure presented as the issuer's own.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The verb is registered in `verbs.toml` and robot-docs, and `cargo run -p xtask -- check-all` passes.
- Envelope golden test: the four flags are false; the `no_claim` text and the no-affiliation label are present; BD-329's validator finds no uncited number.
- Without the corpus, the verb exits 8 and names every missing registered file.
- On the gate-fired path, exactly two site cards render.
- Reruns are byte-identical.
- No output text contains a calibration verdict or a ranking.

## Tests and logging
**Unit tests:**
- `test_cli_track_record_usage_errors`: an unknown issuer or a missing `--issuer` exits 2.
- `test_cli_track_record_refuses_without_registered_documents`: exit 8, with the files named.
- `test_track_record_envelope_flags_and_labels`: on synthetic rows.
- `test_track_record_no_uncited_numbers`: BD-329 `citation::uncited` returns empty.
- `test_track_record_gate_fired_renders_two_site_cards`.
- `test_track_record_rerun_byte_identical`.

**Negative controls:**
- `test_track_record_text_has_no_verdict_words`: scans for "calibrated", "beats guidance" and "rank".
- `test_track_record_ranking_request_refuses`.

**Ignored real-file test.** `test_cli_track_record_barrick_real_files` runs in BD-339's CI job (`-p fmine-cli -- --ignored`).
- Per row: `{"event":"track_record_row","site","metric","fy","vintage","guidance_at","outcome_at","state","z_rule"}`.
- Summary: `{"event":"track_record_summary","rows","resolved","unresolved","gate_fired","certificate"}`.

## Close rule
Close only with this subtask's own evidence, as typed references: `test:<crate>::<path>::<fn>`, `commit:<sha7>`, `record:<path>`, `ci:<run-id>@<sha7>` or an E id. Never a shared or generic reason (K.2 finding 4).

Markdown shows Claim IDs, included years and exact reference bounds. Concurrent evidence-cut and price-sensitivity commands are preserved. title: BD-336 [WP-10]: Metallurgical-balance and sampler-record import for the recovery-led GATE-DATA-03 route (§37.3 M2)
description:
_Plan row BD-336 (WP-10). Scope in one line: Metallurgical-balance and sampler-record import for the recovery-led GATE-DATA-03 route_

## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- Plan row's blocked-by list: BD-187
- plan-deps: BD-187   proposed-deps: BD-187, BD-186, BD-137, BD-309; BD-133 for the synthetic e2e only
- blocks: BD-204 (existing edge, K.6)

Type and priority rationale: priority: 2 (it blocks BD-204 on the 29-bead critical path, but no site data can exist before GATE-DATA-01 at month 4; it must be ready by month 6)

## Background and why it matters
The M2 pilot (plan §37.3) prefers **Lumwana**, Barrick's only wholly owned operating mine. There the finding is **recovery-led**, not grade-led:
- every 2025–26 quarter sits 1.7–2.7 points below the 2013–22 grade–recovery relation (INFERENCE, E566);
- that is 2.4–3.4% of output, roughly $30–57M/yr at $4.00–5.50/lb (INFERENCE, E567);
- the public metal balance reproduces the printed recovery within ±1.5 points, so the gap is not a print artefact (E127).

The pre-registered deliverable attributes the grade-normalised gap among three causes: measurement (head and tail sampling, assay), ore type (fresh against transitional) and operations.

GATE-DATA-03 therefore has two thresholds (R7-C084, R7-C102; §34.4):
- the **recovery-led** threshold, which is this bead's file set:
  - the monthly metallurgical balance;
  - head, tail and concentrate sampler and assay records;
  - concentrate shipment and settlement assays;
  - fresh/transitional tags on feed;
  - the monthly reconciliation pack;
- the grade-led threshold, which needs block and GC models, dispatch tonnages, surveys and cost-centre extracts.

On the recovery-led route BD-204 does not wait on BD-188, BD-189 or BD-194. It waits on this bead (K.6 adds the edge BD-204 ← BD-336, and with it WP-12 → WP-10). GATE-TOUCH-03 gains a recovery-led variant: parity with the site's monthly metallurgical balance and recovery statement, not with F1/F2/F3.

## Goal
Import the recovery-led file set through the quarantine pipeline, with every column declared. Then reproduce the site's own monthly recovery statement from the imported records: each month is either reproduced within its printed rounding or listed as a cited discrepancy.

## Current state (FACT unless marked)
- No `fmine-plant` crate exists. The P754 balance (BD-177), the flowsheet types (BD-175) and the reconciliation engine (BD-149) are all open.
- `fmine-io` reads XLSX and HTML tables only (`crates/fmine-io/CONTRACT.md` §4; `crates/fmine-io/src/lib.rs:45`). It has no CSV reader. BD-187 (own CSV/Excel readers), BD-185 (quarantine pipeline) and BD-186 (`io_dialects.toml`) are open.
- No site data exist, and site data by month 7 is not assumed (plan §34.4; E599). This bead is an M2 design with no code yet.
- The plan names no bead for GATE-TOUCH-03's recovery-led variant. BD-206 owns GATE-TOUCH-03 only as F1/F2/F3 parity.

## Scope
**In:**
- dialect rows for the five recovery-led file families;
- record types;
- quadruple timestamps;
- parity recomputation against the site statement;
- import reports with explained rejections.

**Out:**
- the reconciliation posterior (BD-207);
- sampler bias models (BD-178);
- the historian and LIMS (GATE-DATA-04);
- any personal data.

## Design (DESIGN)
- **Record types** (in `fmine-plant::import`, layer K2; parsing in `fmine-io`):
  - `MetBalanceMonth{period, streams: [StreamRow{stream: Feed|Concentrate|Tail|Other, dry_t, grades: [{species: CuT|CuAS|Au|…, value, unit}], contained, method: Measured|Calculated|Reconciled}], stated_recovery{value, printed_precision, method_label}}`;
  - `SamplerRecord{sampler_id, stream, lot, increments, cut_interval}`;
  - `AssayRecord{sample_id, lab, method, batch, certificate, crm_results, value, detection_limit}`;
  - `Shipment{lot, wet_t, moisture, dry_t, assays: {seller, buyer, umpire}, settlement}`;
  - `FeedTag{period_or_lot, fresh_fraction, transitional_fraction}`.
- **Declarations and stamps.**
  - Every column has a dialect row giving unit, basis (wet or dry; total or acid-soluble Cu) and support. A column without one stays `UNREGISTERED` (FMINE-REF-107).
  - Raw tokens are kept.
  - Every record carries a `QuadTemporalStamp`.
- **Quarantine.** Bytes land read-only in `ImportQuarantineRegion` (no TIME, RANDOM or REMOTE), each citing its CAS digest. Rejections are explained one by one in the import report.
- **Personal data.** Sampler and lab logs can name operators. A dialect row marks such columns `Personal`. They are never imported, and Zambia's DPA 2021 s.70 keeps personal data in country (E514).
- **Parity.** For each month, recompute:
  - contained metal per stream (dry t × grade);
  - the mass-measured recovery, conc metal ÷ feed metal;
  - the two-product recovery, R = c(f − t) / (f(c − t));
  - check-in against check-out, kept separate as MCF in and out (§17.5).

  Compare the result with the stated recovery on its printed rounding interval, using the statement's declared method:
  - declared method reproduced: state i;
  - no method declared and exactly one formula reproduces: state ii (reconstructed);
  - both or neither formula reproduces: state iv, or state iii with a certificate.

  The import never adds a tolerance that the site did not state.
- **Worked example (synthetic, labelled).** Feed is 2,000,000 t at 0.60% Cu (12,000 t Cu). Concentrate is 50,000 t at 22% (11,000 t). Tail is 1,950,000 t at 0.05% (975 t).
  - The mass-measured recovery is 11,000 ÷ 12,000 = 91.67%.
  - The two-product recovery is 22 × 0.55 ÷ (0.60 × 21.95) = 91.88%.
  - 25 t of metal is unaccounted.

  A statement printing 91.9% matches only the two-product method, so the month is state ii if no method is declared. A statement printing 91.7% matches only the mass method.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each of the five file families from the pilot site imports with zero `UNREGISTERED` columns used in parity, and each rejection is explained.
- Each historical month (the target is 2024Q1–2027Q1; §37.3) has a parity state. Every month not in state i or ii names its certificate or the document that would close it.
- The import report and the parity table regenerate byte-identically from the same snapshot.
- No personal column crosses the import boundary.

## Tests
- **Unit:**
  - the two formulas against BD-137's P754 and two-product fixtures;
  - rounding-interval comparison;
  - wet-to-dry conversion with moisture.
- **Property:**
  - permuting the order of rows and files leaves parity unchanged;
  - unit relabelling (t and kt; % and g/t where valid) leaves states unchanged.
- **Known answers:** the synthetic month above; a synthetic site pack from BD-133 with seeded head-sampler bias, where parity must still reproduce the site's (biased) statement, because parity is not truth.
- **Negative and mutation:**
  - drop a column's dialect row: refused;
  - swap the conc and tail grades: a state iii certificate appears;
  - a statement with an unstated method: no silent choice;
  - an operator-name column: refused at import.
- **e2e:** `fmine import` over a synthetic Lumwana-dialect snapshot. Structured logs per file (digest, rows, rejections) and per month (state, formula, interval).

## Risks, kill criteria and fallbacks
- **The site's balance uses reconciled masses that we cannot reproduce from raw records.** Import the reconciled balance as an `Assertion` with parity on its own arithmetic, and flag that raw-to-reconciled parity is unavailable.
- **The site supplies only PDFs.** Use cited-mode entry by two readers.
- **Lumwana declines.** The bead still serves the alternates; North Mara is grade-led and does not need it.

## Recommended plan changes
1. Add BD-186 (dialects) and BD-137 (P754 fixtures) as dependencies. Parity needs both.
2. Add BD-309 (stamps) as a dependency, after the stamp shape is fixed (see BD-344's note on the plan–code field mismatch).
3. Give GATE-TOUCH-03's recovery-led variant an owner. Either widen BD-206's done-when to "F1/F2/F3 parity, or monthly metallurgical-balance parity via BD-336", or add a small bead.

## References
- Plan: §37.3 M2 (lines 7672–7740); §34.4 GATE-DATA-03 (7352–7386); §17.5 (3205–3236); §32.1; K.6; bead row line 8182.
- Evidence: E127, E514, E566, E567, E570, E599 (`planning/research/W4_m2_site_and_data_access.md:609–642`).
- Claims: R7-C084, R7-C102.
- Code: `crates/fmine-io/CONTRACT.md`.
acceptance_criteria:
Plan done-when (§39 row BD-336): Site's monthly balance and recovery statement imported with parity

- Each of the five file families from the pilot site imports with zero `UNREGISTERED` columns used in parity, and each rejection is explained.
- Each historical month (the target is 2024Q1–2027Q1; §37.3) has a parity state. Every month not in state i or ii names its certificate or the document that would close it.
- The import report and the parity table regenerate byte-identically from the same snapshot.
- No personal column crosses the import boundary.

K.6 edge kept: bd-204 <- BD-336. The recovery-led GATE-TOUCH-03 variant now has its own bead, which depends on this one.

title: NEW [WP-01]: GATE-FSIM-DRIFT: quarterly diff of every lifted frankensim region against its pinned commit
description:
## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- plan-deps: none (plan §27 defines the gate; no bead row owns it)   proposed-deps: NEW-lift-provenance-truth
- blocks: none

Type and priority rationale: priority: 3 (M1 suite gate; little to diff until NEW-lift-provenance-truth leaves only true lifts with pinned commits)

## Background and why it matters
FrankenMining lifts code from the sibling engine FrankenSim instead of depending on it (plan §27.1: "Lift-only", FD-FSIM-00; any Cargo dependency waits for GATE-FSIM-RECONV). Lifted code can drift from upstream bug fixes. Plan §27 defines **GATE-FSIM-DRIFT** (quarterly): diff each lifted source at frankensim HEAD against its pinned commit; any upstream change inside a lifted region opens a bead within 10 working days; the decision (re-lift, or no-op with a reason) is recorded. Plan F8 lists it as the control for "lifted-code drift or an upstream bug". No bead row owns it (§39), and the suite table puts it at M1.

FACT (2026-10-29 research, recorded in NEW-lift-provenance-truth): five of the eight files registered as "lifted" share at most two lines with their claimed upstream file, and the rand row hashes `lib.rs` while the code came from `philox.rs`. A drift check over false provenance would diff unrelated files. So this bead waits for that correction.

## Process-rule answers (AGENTS RULE 0.1)
1. Consumer: the agent who re-lifts, and the M1 suite gate record.
2. Gate enforced: GATE-FSIM-DRIFT.
3. Defect class: a known upstream bug fix not carried into a lifted copy (plan F8).
4. Retirement: when no lifted frankensim region remains (all replaced by own code or by a Cargo dependency after GATE-FSIM-RECONV).

## Goal
`cargo run -p xtask -- check-lift-drift --upstream <path-to-frankensim-checkout>` reads `registries/lifts.toml` (source repo, path, line range or symbol, pinned commit, lifted blake3), diffs each region between the pinned commit and upstream HEAD, and prints one line per lift: `unchanged`, `changed (n lines)` with the diff, or `missing upstream`. A scheduled CI job runs it quarterly and fails on any `changed` row without a recorded decision.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Every lifts.toml row is checked; a seeded upstream change in a test fixture repository is reported as `changed`, and an unrelated change outside the region as `unchanged`.
2. A decision file (or the bead it opens) records re-lift or no-op with reason per changed row; the CI job passes only when every changed row has one.
3. Runs without network access when given a local checkout; quotes upstream commits, never working-tree state (frankensim's working tree has had uncommitted deletions: E824).

## Tests
Unit tests on region extraction (line range and symbol); an e2e over a temporary git repository built in the test with two commits; structured output, one JSON line per lift.

## Risks
Keep it one xtask subcommand plus one CI schedule; no dashboard, no new registry beyond fields lifts.toml already needs.

## References
Plan §27.1–27.2, §31.4 suite table (line ~7344), F8 (line ~6101), GATE-FSIM-DRIFT text (line ~6225); FD-FSIM-00; E824; NEW-lift-provenance-truth.

## E2E test script and logging
- **Logging.** The e2e over a temporary git repository emits one JSON line per lift: path, upstream path, pinned commit, head commit, `unchanged|changed|moved|deleted`, diff line count. One summary line. A `changed` lift names the hunk headers.

title: NEW [WP-19]: LP-guided OMF schedule with a certified upper bound (fmine-io omf::pit -> toposort::lp + fmine-lp PDLP)
description:
## Why
The LP-guided schedule pipeline exists only in the MineLib harnesses (`crates/xtask/tests/cpit_schedule.rs`, `pcpsp_schedule.rs`). It runs `toposort::lp::relaxation`, then fmine-lp PDLP, `Shares`, `lp::starts` (six TopoSort starts from LP thresholds and medians) and `lp::incumbent` (local search from each, best kept). fmine-optimize cannot call fmine-lp (same layer E), and fmine-cli is over budget. bd-fr8x schedules OMF block models from a caller's ranking only. With the LP, an OMF model gets MineLib-grade starts and PDLP's certified dual bound, so the schedule's gap to the best possible is known.

## Scope
In fmine-io `omf::pit` (V; fmine-lp is E, so the edge runs downward):
- `PitModel::lp_schedule(&ScheduleSpec, &PdlpOptions) -> LpSchedule`. It builds the same ScheduleProblem as `schedule` and the relaxation at decimals 0, so the LP is in units of 1/per_unit. It then runs PDLP `solve`, `Shares` from x, `starts` and `incumbent`.
- `LpSchedule::{problem, factors, lp, upper_bound, incumbent}`. `upper_bound` is minus PDLP's certified bound: no schedule's discounted value, with factors (1+r)^-t in f64, exceeds it.
- `schedule` and `lp_schedule` share a private `schedule_problem`.

## Acceptance criteria
1. E2E on the bd-joiv section with the bd-fr8x capacities: the incumbent reaches the same hand optimum, passes `toposort::check`, and its f64 NPV lies at or below `upper_bound` (Some).
2. A refusal passes through: limits for the wrong number of periods (207).
3. Planted bug: building the shares from a zero vector instead of PDLP's x changes the starts (checked through the logged starts or the result).
4. CONTRACTs are updated (fmine-io, fmine-optimize §10 for toposort::lp, fmine-lp §10 for BD-251's caller).

## Not in scope
PCPSP destinations; LP caching; CLI.

title: BD-353 [WP-14]: Compensation-formula exposure: exact piecewise evaluator of a scheme formula over admitted metric definitions and rounding intervals; synthetic first, then one publicly disclosed formula; no personal data
description:
_Plan row BD-353 (WP-14). Scope in one line: Compensation-formula exposure: an exact piecewise evaluator over admitted metric definitions, with no personal data_

## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- Plan row's blocked-by list: BD-340, BD-061
- plan-deps: BD-340, BD-061   proposed-deps: BD-340, BD-061, BD-332 (metric vintage keys)
- blocks: none

Type and priority rationale: priority: 3 (serves the compensation-committee reader R7 added; M1 synthetic slice; the public case may end in an ambiguity warning)

## Background and why it matters
R7 added the compensation (remuneration) committee as a reader (§3; K.3 #2; R7-C139, R7-C140). Its question is not what a metric *is*, but whether the admitted definitions, adjustments and rounding support **one** scheme-level performance factor, or whether the ambiguity can cross a threshold.

**Why a point is not enough.** A step or kink in a scheme turns a small metric ambiguity into a large factor ambiguity. A capped portion can absorb a large change. A midpoint evaluation hides both.

**What the plan already has.** §23.6 prices the economic sacrifice of KPI constraints. It does not evaluate the scheme function itself. The duel's Codex blind spot BS-COD-02 (self 740; orchestrator 650; K.5 row 17) proposes exactly that, synthetic first.

**The public case (FACT unless marked).**
- Barrick's 2026 Circular scorecard gives gold AISC an 18.75% weight. The row prints $1,565/oz, $1,352/oz and $1,423/oz (E605).
- The reported FY2025 AISC was $1,637/oz (E607).
- The Circular promises to disclose adjustments, but shows none for AISC. The $1,637 → $1,423 bridge is therefore undisclosed (INFERENCE, E608; OPEN-BULL-1).
- GEO in the scorecard uses fixed reserve prices of $1,500/oz and $3.25/lb (E606), so that component's basis is reproducible.

## Goal
A pure, exact evaluator of a scheme formula over admitted metric definitions and rounding intervals. It returns the *image set* of the scheme index and the clause and branch behind each possible value. It works on a synthetic scheme first, then on one publicly disclosed formula if its terms suffice. Otherwise it gives an ambiguity warning naming the missing clause.

## Current state (FACT)
- No Helm crates exist (`fmine-capital`, `fmine-econ`). `fmine-metrics` holds versioned decks and GEO (`crates/fmine-metrics/src/lib.rs:88–130`). BD-061 (the metric engine) is closed with the generic reason. BD-340 exists only in the plan text.
- `ExactQty` has mul and div only. Exact rational add and compare must come from BD-340's type (`crates/fmine-units/src/lib.rs:275–332`).
- No scheme data, no evaluator. This is an M1 design.

## Scope
**In:**
- a scheme specification: components, weights, schedules, inequality direction, caps, and the metric definition id plus vintage plus adjustment policy;
- an exact piecewise evaluator over intervals and branches;
- breakpoint enumeration;
- clause attribution;
- one public capture attempt.

**Out:**
- salaries, grants, individual achievement, names, or any person-linked id;
- estimating anyone's pay;
- deciding whether a restatement changes an award or triggers clawback;
- pricing safety gates (hard, never priced; G-HELM-1);
- payroll administration.

## Design (DESIGN)
- **Spec.** A `SchemeSpec` lists `components[k]`, each with:
  - `weight` (exact rational);
  - `metric: MetricRef{definition_id, vintage, adjustment_policy}`;
  - `direction` (HigherBetter or LowerBetter);
  - `schedule`: breakpoints with payout factors and an interpolation rule (Step or Linear);
  - an explicit inequality at every breakpoint (≥ or >);
  - `cap` and `floor`.

  The spec text and its structured reading carry a role-reviewed version. An unknown adjustment policy stays `Unresolved`. It never defaults to the public non-GAAP definition.
- **Evaluation.**
  - Each component's admitted input is a set of intervals, one per definition branch, each widened by its rounding interval.
  - The image of a piecewise-linear schedule over an interval is computed exactly:
    - evaluate the interval endpoints and every breakpoint inside the interval;
    - for Step rules, add both one-sided limits at each step.
  - The output is a finite union of points and intervals. Rules may be non-monotone; endpoints alone are not assumed to suffice.
  - Components combine by Minkowski sum over the weighted images, with branches kept apart.
- **Output.**
  - The image set.
  - Its breakpoints crossed.
  - For each piece, the branch and clause responsible.
  - The output is never collapsed to a midpoint, and a range that straddles a threshold is never printed as a point.
- **Known answer (INFERENCE; BS-COD-02).** Fixed components contribute 0.75. One component of weight 0.25 pays 0 below a normalised achievement of 0.90 and 1 at or above it (≥). The admitted achievement is [0.89, 0.91].
  - The image is **{0.75, 1.00}**: two points, not the interval 0.75–1.00.
  - The midpoint answer, 1.00, would hide the threshold.
- **Public attempt.**
  - Capture the 2026 Circular's scorecard formula and definitions by two-reader cited transcription.
  - Admit the GEO component if its schedule and interpolation rule are stated. That they are stated has not been checked here (OPEN).
  - For gold AISC, the expected result is the ambiguity warning: "adjustment from reported $1,637 to scored $1,423 not disclosed (E608)", with the Circular page that would close it. No factor is printed for that component.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every threshold boundary in the synthetic schemes is enumerated, and no range across a threshold is reported as a point (K.5 row 17).
- The synthetic known answer above reproduces as a two-point set.
- The public attempt either reproduces the disclosed factor with hashes and locators, or names precisely the clause that prevents reproduction.
- A data-scope check finds no field in the spec or the outputs that can hold a person identifier.

## Tests
- **Unit:**
  - step and linear schedules;
  - ≥ against > at ties;
  - caps and floors;
  - lower-is-better metrics (AISC);
  - Minkowski sum over components.
- **Exhaustive:** a small rational grid evaluated against an independently authored rule table, covering every breakpoint, tie, cap, overlapping branch, wrong metric vintage and rounding interval that straddles a threshold.
- **Property and metamorphic:**
  - a pure unit change (for example $/oz expressed in cents) preserves the image;
  - narrowing the input never enlarges the image.
- **Negative:**
  - an unresolved adjustment policy yields `Unresolved`, not a number;
  - a wrong metric vintage is refused.
- **e2e:** an evaluation of a synthetic scheme, with structured logs `{component, branch, interval, breakpoints_crossed, image}`.

## Risks, kill criteria and fallbacks
- **Nothing reproducible.** If no disclosed formula can be reproduced from public terms, ship the ambiguity warning only (K.5).
- **Out of bounds.** Kill if the useful workflow needs personal remuneration data or automatic legal interpretation. Do not build a generic compensation engine.
- **Never:**
  - name an executive;
  - estimate an award;
  - say an award was wrong;
  - imply any Barrick affiliation.

## References
- Plan: §3 (compensation-committee row), §23.6 (lines 5193–5213), OPEN-BULL-1 (4789), K.3 #2, K.5 row 17, bead row line 8262.
- Duel: `planning/duel/WIZARD_BLINDSPOTS_COD.md:104–175` (BS-COD-02).
- Evidence: E605–E608 (`planning/research/W5_figure_verification.md:322–329`).
- Claims: R7-C139, R7-C140.

description:
_Plan row BD-321 (WP-03). Scope in one line: Remove both silent fallbacks; synthetic lane for the stand-in; real-file run (K.2 step 1)_

## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- Plan row's blocked-by list: —
- plan-deps: —   proposed-deps: —
- blocks: BD-322 (plan)

Type and priority rationale: priority: 0 (K.2 pre-push step 1; DONE in commit 543df53, closed with its own evidence)

## Background and why it matters
Round 7 (plan Appendix K.2, finding 1; claims R7-C001, R7-C011, R7-C058, R7-C059, R7-C065) found that the first M0 commit (`68e7091`) did not read Barrick's data at all.
- Every figure that `fmine assure public --issuer barrick` printed came from a workbook built in code (a "stand-in") or from literals.
- When a registered file was missing or unreadable, the reader silently substituted the stand-in, file by file, and exited 0.
- With the real workbooks present under the expected names, the command refused (FMINE-REF-502, no "Gold AISC" sheet).
- Changing an input cell left the output and the state root byte-identical. The output did not depend on the inputs at all.

Finding 2 (R7-C002–R7-C006, R7-C054, R7-C159) showed the stand-in's figures were wrong as Barrick figures:
- FY2025 AISC printed 1,638 against a published $1,637/oz.
- 3,255 is attributable production, not ounces sold (3,318).
- The reserve-replacement inputs had been solved to hit 190% and 504%.
- None of the stand-in's 41 explicit values sat at a published coordinate.

Under the owner's loss function, a wrong figure under an issuer's name is the costliest M0 failure. That is why this was step 1 of the pre-push list.

## Goal
1. A missing or unreadable registered file makes the run exit non-zero, naming the file.
2. No in-code workbook can be mistaken for an issuer's data. Synthetic data run in a separate lane whose output says `synthetic` and can never count toward GATE-BULL-01 (the M0 gate on reproducing Barrick's published figures).
3. The four stand-in tests are replaced by labelled synthetic tests plus a real-file run. None is deleted or weakened.

## What was done (FACT, commit 543df53, 2026-10-29)
**`fmine-io`: both fallbacks removed.**
- `build_canonical_barrick_xlsx_bytes()` is gone (`crates/fmine-io/src/zip_inflate.rs`).

**`fmine-public`: refusal and synthetic lane.**
- `load_registered_sources` refuses with FMINE-REF-502 (exit 8). The refusal names every missing, altered or unreadable registered file: "N of 18 registered barrick workbooks unusable under …; missing: …; digest mismatch: …; unreadable: …".
- `synthetic.rs` holds the synthetic lane: invented sites "Site A–G" and "Region North", with seeded known answers for every state of the identity ledger.
- `Lane::Synthetic` reports `"lane":"synthetic"` and `gate_eligible:false`.

**`fmine-cli`.**
- `fmine assure public --synthetic` runs the synthetic lane.
- `--issuer` plus `--synthetic`, a missing `--issuer`, and an unknown issuer are usage errors (exit 2).

**`fmine-metrics`.**
- The mislabelled "Barrick" tests (GEO, reserve replacement, LMDI) are relabelled synthetic, with honest known answers.
- The price decks were corrected to the 2026 Circular (E606).

## Acceptance Criteria
_the plan's done-when, with evidence_
1. "A missing or unreadable registered file exits non-zero naming it":
   - `fmine-public` `missing_corpus_refuses_naming_every_registered_file`;
   - `fmine-public/tests/registry.rs` `altered_registered_file_is_refused_with_both_digests`;
   - `fmine-io` `test_missing_file_is_an_error_never_a_stand_in`;
   - the `fmine-cli` refusal test (exit 8, names `Barrick_Q2_2026_AISC.xlsx`).
2. "Synthetic output is labelled and excluded": `fmine-public` `synthetic_lane_reproduces_every_seeded_answer`, plus the `fmine-cli` synthetic end-to-end test. Both assert `lane=synthetic` and `gate_eligible=false`.
3. Real-file run: the ignored test `barrick_real_files_match_the_independent_reader` passes locally on the 18 workbooks (MOR_CASE E820–E822).

## Tests
- All the tests above are in the workspace suite, and `cargo test --workspace` is green: 71 passed, 2 ignored (run 2026-10-29).

- **Live-dependency proof.** That every scored value depends on its inputs is proven by BD-338. This bead only removed the fallbacks.
