title: BD-328 [WP-06]: Refusal registry as the single source: plan, registry and compiled catalogue agree; family → exit-code table (§30.1)
description:
_Plan row BD-328 (WP-06). Scope in one line: One refusal registry — `registries/refusals.toml` is the single source; the compiled catalogue is generated from it; plan §8.4/§25.6/§31.3, registry and catalogue agree; family → exit-code table (§30.1); usage errors exit 2_

## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- Plan row's blocked-by list: —
- plan-deps: — (root)   proposed-deps: none hard. Subtask 1 needs an owner decision (plan amendment for the codes the plan lacks); everything else can proceed against the plan as written.
- blocks: BD-327's refusal-code check becoming an error; reopened BD-039 (re-close on this bead's evidence)

Type and priority rationale: priority: 1 (agents and operators read these codes today: a formula-error cell in a Barrick workbook refuses with the code the plan reserves for "unknown reactive ground → no ANFO plan"; only 4 of 25 codes mean the same thing in all three places)

## Background and why it matters
A refusal is the product's way of saying "no number", so its code is part of the public contract. The robot envelope (FMT-ENV-1, §30.1) carries `{code, what, fix}` and an exit code. Agents branch on both. The plan defines the codes in §8.4, restates some in §25.6 and §31.3, and since round 7 says (§30.1):
- `registries/refusals.toml` is the single source;
- the compiled catalogue is generated from it;
- a CI check compares code, meaning and exit code in both directions.

Round 7 found that the three disagree. Of the plan's 25 codes, only 102, 103, 108 and 504 mean the same thing in the plan, the registry and the catalogue (R7-C080, K.2 finding 7). The only automated check verifies that each catalogue code is present in the registry, not its meaning or exit code.

## Goal
- One registry row per code.
- A generated Rust catalogue whose codes form a closed enum, so an unregistered code cannot compile.
- Every call site uses the code whose plan meaning matches the condition.
- Exit codes follow the §30.1 family table.
- A CI check fails on any drift between plan, registry, catalogue and contracts.

## Current state (FACT)
- **Plan §8.4** (lines 765–769), 25 codes:
  - 101 conservation; 102 support mismatch; 103 non-additive average; 104 non-identifiable attribution; 105 basis mismatch; 106 unregistered or incompatible CRS; 107 undeclared unit/basis/time zone on import; 108 assay lookahead;
  - 201 no claim in domain; 202 not observable; 203 outside AOA; 204 unbudgeted unknowns; 205 calibration required for decision-grade use;
  - 301 MNPI wall; 302 venture wall; 303 residency; 304 missing human authority token;
  - 401 unknown reactive ground; 402 unknown PAG; 403 unknown moisture vs TML; 404 stale TSF instrumentation;
  - 501 FA refusal relayed; 502 stale anchor; 503 sibling capability unavailable; 504 uncured backfill.
- **§30.1 family rule:** 1xx → 3; 2xx → 3; 3xx → 7; 4xx → 7; 5xx → 8 (digest or signature) or 6 (stale anchor). Usage errors → 2, with no code. A missing or unreadable registered input is "a typed refusal that names the file, never a digest-mismatch code".
- **`registries/refusals.toml`:** 22 rows. **`REFUSAL_CATALOG`** (`crates/fmine-evidence/src/lib.rs:70-203`): 22 rows. `Refusal::from_code` falls back to an unregistered `FMINE-REF-000`, exit 2, for any unknown string (lib.rs:27-32).
- **Comparison** (meaning; exit code in brackets; ✓ = all three agree):

| Code | Plan | Registry | Catalogue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 101 | conservation | conservation [3] | CRS mismatch [3] |
| 102 ✓ | support mismatch | same [3] | same [3] |
| 103 ✓ | non-additive average | same [3] | same [3] |
| 104 | non-identifiable attribution | same + unbridged layer [3] | density missing [3] |
| 105 | basis mismatch | same [3] | fraction outside [0,1]; **fix says "Clamp or re-normalize"** [3] |
| 106 | unregistered/incompatible CRS | unregistered CRS or out of hull [3] | out of hull [3] |
| 107 | undeclared unit/basis/tz | same [3] | chemical basis mismatch [3] |
| 108 ✓ | assay lookahead | same [3] | same [3] |
| 201 | no claim in domain | missing UuTerm [4] | mass-balance discrepancy [4] |
| 202 | not observable | late forecast registration [4] | journal not zero-sum [4] |
| 203 | outside AOA | disclosure roll-up [4] | disclosure roll-up [4] |
| 204, 205 | unbudgeted unknowns; calibration required | — | — |
| 301 | MNPI wall | MNPI wall *or* non-PD covariance [7] | non-PD covariance [5] |
| 302 | venture wall | same [7] | FoS/PoF envelope [5] |
| 303 | residency | same [7] | TARP red [5] |
| 304 | missing human token | LP infeasible [5] | LP infeasible [5] |
| 401 | unknown reactive ground | stale lease / Red claim [6] | Green on placeholder [6] |
| 402 | unknown PAG | confidentiality export [6] | same as registry [6] |
| 403 | unknown moisture vs TML | forecast mutation [6] | same as registry [6] |
| 404 | stale TSF instrumentation | DecisionCard missing UU [6] | same as registry [6] |
| 501 | FA refusal relayed | direct actuation [7] | bench precedence [7] |
| 502 | stale anchor | digest mismatch or missing file [8] | digest mismatch [8] |
| 503 | sibling unavailable | — | — |
| 504 ✓ | uncured backfill | same [7] | same [7] |

- **Exit codes:** 10 of the registry's 22 rows break the family rule: 201–203 (4, not 3), 304 (5, not 7), 401–404 (6, not 7), 501 (7) and 504 (7). The 504 case is a plan inconsistency: it is a safety refusal numbered in the 5xx family.
- **Misuse at call sites** (20 `Refusal::from_code` calls plus the `code()` mappers in fmine-crs, -time and -units):
  - `fmine-public/src/lib.rs:71-84`: a workbook formula-error or text cell refuses with **401** (plan: reactive ground).
  - `fmine-public/src/lib.rs:191` and `fmine-cli`: a missing registered file refuses with **502** (plan: stale anchor; §30.1: never a digest code).
  - `fmine-numerics/src/lib.rs:21,35`: a non-SPD Cholesky refuses with **301** (plan: MNPI wall; §29.6 routes failed linear solves to 2xx).
  - `fmine-calib/src/lib.rs:52-98`: late registration, duplicates, unknown ids and `std_dev <= 0` all use **403** (plan: moisture vs TML).
  - `fmine-crs/src/lib.rs:28`: CRS mismatch uses **101** (plan: 106).
  - `fmine-units/src/lib.rs:33`: chemical basis uses **107** (plan §25: 105, line 5676).
  - `fmine-claim`: 401, 402 and 404 are used for calibration, confidentiality and UU (plan: 205, 3xx, 204).
- **Contracts** cite codes that exist nowhere else: 109, 110 (fmine-claim) and 206 (fmine-units).
- **Usage errors already exit 2 with no code** (`fmine-cli/src/lib.rs:59-71`, `test_cli_usage_errors`). Keep this.

## Scope
**In:**
- the plan amendment request for the missing meanings (subtask 1);
- registry schema and rewrite;
- the generator and drift check;
- the closed `RefusalCode` enum;
- migrating every call site and contract;
- tests.

**Out:**
- new guards (each guard bead adds its own refusal);
- the MCP/TUI surfaces.

## Design
**Missing meanings (DESIGN; needs the owner's plan amendment, because ids are never renumbered, §0.3).** The code needs refusals the plan does not name. R7-C093 and C100 identify digest mismatch and forecast-ledger mutation as the genuine gaps. Proposal, appended to §8.4:
- **505** artifact digest or signature mismatch → exit 8.
- **506** registered input missing or unreadable (names every file) → exit 5, "foundation I/O".
- **206** forecast registered after its freeze or resolution → exit 3. This is INV-008 at registration.
- **507** frozen record mutation attempted → exit 6, "conflict".
- **207** numerical certificate failed (non-SPD, solver residual) → exit 3, per §29.6's "FMINE-REF-2xx".
- **208** source cell unusable (formula error or text where a number is required) → exit 3.
- **109** value outside its physical domain (fraction outside [0,1]) → exit 3. It refuses; it never clamps.
- LP infeasibility is not a refusal: §29.6 routes it to the three-gap ledger.
- 504 keeps its number with an explicit exit-7 exception in §30.1.
- Until the owner amends the plan, the registry holds these rows with `status = "proposed"`, and the drift check reports them as warnings.

**Registry schema** (`schema_version = 2`):
```toml
[[refusal]]
code = "FMINE-REF-101"; family = "1xx"; key = "conservation"; exit_code = 3
plan_text = "conservation"          # verbatim §8.4 phrase; the check finds "101 conservation" in the plan
what = "…"; fix = "…"; status = "active"   # active | proposed | reserved
```

**Generator.**
- `xtask gen-refusals` writes `crates/fmine-evidence/src/refusal_catalog.rs`: `pub enum RefusalCode { Conservation101, … }` plus `const CATALOG: [RefusalSpec; N]`. The file is generated and committed, and carries a header with the registry's sha256.
- `xtask check-refusals` regenerates in memory and diffs, and fails on any byte difference.
- No `build.rs`, so S0 keeps no build-time I/O (L-2).
- `Refusal::from_code(&str, …)` is replaced by `Refusal::new(RefusalCode, detail)`. The `FMINE-REF-000` fallback is deleted (code removal only; no file is deleted).

**Drift check (`check-refusals`):**
- (a) Every §8.4 code has a registry row whose `"{nnn} {plan_text}"` occurs verbatim in that family's §8.4 row. Every active registry row maps back the same way.
- (b) `exit_code` follows the family table, or is a listed exception (504).
- (c) Every `FMINE-REF-\d{3}` token in `crates/**/*.rs` and `crates/*/CONTRACT.md` is a registry code.
- (d) No `fix` text contains "clamp" or "re-normalize", to enforce "refuse, never clamp".

**Call-site migration (DESIGN; final numbers after subtask 1).**

| Call site | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| formula-error or text cell | 401 | 208 |
| missing registered file | 502 | 506 |
| altered file | 502 | 505 |
| non-SPD Cholesky | 301 | 207 |
| late forecast | 403 | 206 |
| outcome overwrite | 403 | 507 |
| CRS mismatch | 101 | 106 |
| chemical basis | 107 | 105 |
| Green on placeholder or failed calibration | 401 | 205 |
| missing UU | 404 | 204 |
| confidentiality export | 402 | 301, or a 3xx row the owner adds |
| `std_dev <= 0` | 403 | 109 |
| units fraction or moisture outside [0,1] (`fmine-units/src/lib.rs:32`) | 105 | 109 |

Each move updates its test's expected code. For example, `test_cli_assure_public_refuses_without_registered_files` changes from `(8, "refused")` to `(5, "refused")`, and the refusal must still name all 18 registered files (`crates/fmine-public/src/sources.rs`).

**Worked example.** Today the Q2 2026 Mine Stats workbook has 1,092 formula-error cells (E820). If a public Claim were built from one, the envelope would read `FMINE-REF-401` with exit 6, the text "Epistemic gate refuses Green status…", and a plan meaning of "unknown reactive ground → no ANFO plan". An agent reading the plan would conclude that blasting is involved. After this bead, it reads `FMINE-REF-208`, exit 3, "source cell unusable: formula error '#REF!' at <sheet>!<cell>".

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `check-refusals` passes in CI. Plan, registry and catalogue agree on 25 of 25 §8.4 codes, plus every owner-approved addition.
2. Catalogue and registry are byte-consistent (the generator diff is empty).
3. `grep -rn "FMINE-REF-000"` returns nothing. `Refusal` cannot be built from an unregistered code: a compile-fail doctest shows this.
4. Every exit code follows §30.1 or is a listed exception. Usage errors exit 2 with no code; `test_cli_usage_errors` stays green.
5. No `fix` text suggests clamping.
6. Contracts cite only registered codes, so BD-327's check can turn its warning into an error.

## Tests
- **Unit:** generator golden output for a three-row fixture registry; a drift check fixture for each of rules (a)–(d), positive and negative.
- **Mutation:** change one registry `exit_code` and require `check-refusals` to fail; change one catalogue line by hand and require the diff to fail.
- **Per call site:** each migrated refusal has a test asserting `(code, exit_code)`.
- **e2e (CLI):**
  - `fmine assure public --issuer barrick` on an empty workspace → exit 5 and code 506, naming 18 files.
  - With one altered file → exit 8, code 505, both digests.
  - `--issuer newmont` → exit 2, no refusal object (R7-C080's countermodel previously exited 6 with 401).
  - Each run logs one NDJSON line, and the test parses it.

## Risks, kill criteria and fallbacks
- **The owner declines the new codes.** Fall back to the nearest plan code with a precise `what`, and record the mismatch under BD-327's Known gaps. Never invent codes outside the registry.
- **Exit-code changes break agent scripts.** None exist outside this repository at M0; announce the change in CHANGELOG/README.
- **Never** let a refusal text imply a safety condition that does not hold. Never clamp.

## Subtasks
1. **Plan amendment request.** A one-page decision note for the owner covering the proposed codes 109, 205–208, 505–507, the 504 exception and LP infeasibility, plus the §8.4 and §30.1 edits. Acceptance: owner decision recorded (decision id). Deps: none.
2. **Registry v2 and generator.** Schema, rewrite, `gen-refusals`, `check-refusals`, `RefusalCode`. Acceptance: criteria 1, 2 and 5 for the active rows. Deps: none; proposed rows can wait on 1.
3. **Call-site and contract migration.** Move the 20 calls and 3 mappers; update contracts and tests. Acceptance: criteria 3, 4 and 6. Deps: 2 (and 1 for the proposed codes).

## References
- Plan §8.4 (lines 758–769), §25.6 (5759–5762), §29.6 linear-solve rule, §30.1 (6728–6774), §31.3 (7002–7008), BD-328 row (8082), K.2 finding 7, K.3 item 16.
- R7-C080, R7-C092, R7-C093, R7-C100. E820.
- Files: `registries/refusals.toml`, `crates/fmine-evidence/src/lib.rs:10-210`, `crates/fmine-registry/src/lib.rs:87-97`, `crates/fmine-public/src/lib.rs:71-84,191`, `crates/fmine-numerics/src/lib.rs:17-35`, `crates/fmine-calib/src/lib.rs:41-105`, `crates/fmine-crs/src/lib.rs:24-46`, `crates/fmine-units/src/lib.rs:11-51`, `crates/*/CONTRACT.md`.

title: BD-328.S1 [WP-06]: Plan amendment request
description:
## Context
Subtask S1 of BD-328: "BD-328 [WP-06]: Refusal registry as the single source: plan, registry and compiled catalogue agree; family → exit-code table (§30.1)". The parent bead carries the full background, current state, design, tests and risks; read it first (`br show <parent>`; the parent link is set).

**Parent goal.** - One registry row per code.
- A generated Rust catalogue whose codes form a closed enum, so an unregistered code cannot compile.
- Every call site uses the code whose plan meaning matches the condition.
- Exit codes follow the §30.1 family table.
- A CI check fails on any drift between plan, registry, catalogue and contracts.

## Work
REVIEW: the subtask says "proposed codes 109, 205–208", but 205 is already a plan code (§8.4: "205 calibration required for decision-grade use"). The new codes are seven: 109, 206, 207, 208, 505, 506 and 507. Plan codes 204, 205 and 503 are missing from the registry; S2 adds them as active rows without needing a decision.

**Deliverable.** A one-page decision note for the owner, committed as `docs/adr/ADR-REFUSALS-01.md` with status "Proposed". `docs/adr/` already holds ADR-RNG-01 and ADR-NAMING-01. The decision id format is OPEN: the owner may prefer a CELL-DEC entry, per NEW-push-deadline-decisions. Codes are never renumbered (§0.3), so the note asks for additions only.

**Contents** (DESIGN, from the parent):
1. **Problem.** Only 4 of 25 §8.4 codes (102, 103, 108, 504) mean the same thing in the plan, `registries/refusals.toml` and `REFUSAL_CATALOG` (`crates/fmine-evidence/src/lib.rs:70-203`) (R7-C080). Give the worked example. The Q2 2026 Mine Stats workbook has 1,092 formula-error cells (E820). A Claim built from one would read FMINE-REF-401, exit 6, which the plan defines as "unknown reactive ground → no ANFO plan".
2. **Proposed additions to §8.4:**
   - 109 value outside its physical domain (refuse, never clamp) → exit 3;
   - 206 forecast registered after freeze or resolution (INV-008) → 3;
   - 207 numerical certificate failed (non-SPD, solver residual; §29.6) → 3;
   - 208 source cell unusable (formula error or text where a number is required) → 3;
   - 505 artifact digest or signature mismatch → 8;
   - 506 registered input missing or unreadable, naming every file → 5;
   - 507 frozen-record mutation attempted → 6.
3. **§30.1 edits:**
   - 504 keeps its number, with an explicit exit-7 exception: it is a safety refusal numbered in the 5xx family;
   - LP infeasibility is not a refusal; §29.6 routes it to the three-gap ledger;
   - usage errors stay at exit 2 with no code (`test_cli_usage_errors`, `fmine-cli/src/lib.rs:379`).
4. **Questions the code raises that the parent table leaves open** (FACT, grep at 748da79):
   - `claim show` refuses with 502 for "no claim store exists in M0" (`fmine-cli/src/lib.rs:263-268`). Candidates: 503 or 201.
   - `doctor` maps every load error to 502 (`:258`).
   - The synthetic-workbook parse error uses 502 (`fmine-public/src/lib.rs:804`).
   - `cholesky_solve`'s invalid-dimension check uses 301 (`fmine-numerics/src/lib.rs:20`). It is a caller error, not a failed certificate.
   - G-DISC (plan line 751) has no code. `bd-306n.3` needs one.
   - The confidentiality-export refusal maps to 301, or to a new 3xx row.
   - NEW-fa-sap needs a 1xx trunk-post code (`bd-l7mc.1`) and a 2xx certification refusal. BD-357 needs a 3xx salted-packet code (`bd-kftl.2`).
5. **Fallback if declined.** Use the nearest plan code with a precise `what`, and record the mismatch under BD-327's Known gaps. Never invent a code outside the registry.

**What it must never do:** propose a code whose text implies a safety condition that does not hold, or a `fix` text that suggests clamping.

**Hands over.** The decision id. Once the owner approves, S2 marks the approved rows `status = "active"`; until then they are `"proposed"`. S3 uses the final numbers. The plan edits to §8.4 and §30.1 are applied by whoever the owner names (§0.7 hygiene: E ids, lines ≤ 118 characters, no renumbering).

## Acceptance Criteria
- The owner's decision is recorded with an id (for example `decision:ADR-REFUSALS-01`) and a date. The ADR status changes to "Accepted" or "Rejected", with the list of codes approved.
- The note covers all seven new codes, the 504 exception, LP infeasibility and every open question in point 4.
- No code is renumbered. Every proposed exit code follows the §30.1 table: 3 domain or evidence, 5 foundation I/O, 6 conflict, 7 safety or authorization, 8 verification.

## Tests and logging
This is a decision document, so no Rust test is added. Before the owner sees the note, run these checks and quote them in the close reason:
- `test_proposed_codes_absent_today`: `grep -cE 'FMINE-REF-(109|206|207|208|505|506|507)' registries/refusals.toml` = 0 (verified at 748da79), so no collision.
- `test_plan_codes_missing_from_registry`: 204, 205 and 503 are absent from `registries/refusals.toml` today.
- `test_open_call_sites_still_present`: the three 502 call sites and the 301 dimension check listed in point 4 still exist at the commit.

**Log:** none, because nothing runs. The close reason is `decision:<id>; record:docs/adr/ADR-REFUSALS-01.md`.

## Close rule
Close only with this subtask's own evidence, as typed references: `test:<crate>::<path>::<fn>`, `commit:<sha7>`, `record:<path>`, `ci:<run-id>@<sha7>` or an E id. Never a shared or generic reason (K.2 finding 4).

title: BD-328.S2 [WP-06]: Registry v2 and generator
description:
## Context
Subtask S2 of BD-328: "BD-328 [WP-06]: Refusal registry as the single source: plan, registry and compiled catalogue agree; family → exit-code table (§30.1)". The parent bead carries the full background, current state, design, tests and risks; read it first (`br show <parent>`; the parent link is set).

**Parent goal.** - One registry row per code.
- A generated Rust catalogue whose codes form a closed enum, so an unregistered code cannot compile.
- Every call site uses the code whose plan meaning matches the condition.
- Exit codes follow the §30.1 family table.
- A CI check fails on any drift between plan, registry, catalogue and contracts.

## Work
REVIEW: S2 and S3 should land in one commit, or S2 must leave unchanged the registry rows whose call sites S3 migrates. If S2 rewrites row meanings and exit codes to the plan while the call sites still pass the old codes, the CLI prints wrong text. For example, a missing-UU refusal from fmine-claim would print "no claim in domain", and the exit codes shift: 201–203 go from 4 to 3, 401–404 from 6 to 7.

**Registry v2** (`registries/refusals.toml`: `schema_version = 1`, 22 rows today). Rewrite it to `schema_version = 2` with one row per code:
```toml
[[refusal]]
code = "FMINE-REF-101"
family = "1xx"
key = "conservation"
exit_code = 3
plan_text = "conservation"   # verbatim §8.4 phrase
what = "…"
fix = "…"
status = "active"            # active | proposed | reserved
```
- All 25 §8.4 codes are `active`. This adds 204, 205 and 503, which are missing today.
- S1's seven additions are `proposed` until the owner approves them.
- `fix` text never says "clamp" or "re-normalize". Today's catalogue row 105 says "Clamp or re-normalize".

**Generator.** `cargo run -p xtask -- gen-refusals` writes `crates/fmine-evidence/src/refusal_catalog.rs`. The file contains `pub enum RefusalCode { Conservation101, SupportMismatch102, … }`, `pub const CATALOG: [RefusalSpec; N]`, and a header line with the registry's sha256. The file is generated and committed. There is no `build.rs`, so S0 does no build-time I/O (L-2).

xtask has no dependencies (`crates/xtask/Cargo.toml`). For sha256, add a path dependency on `fmine-core` and use `fmine_core::hash::sha256` (`hash.rs:364`); `check_layers` skips xtask (`lib.rs:226`). Do not depend on `fmine-evidence`: if the generated file broke, xtask could not build to regenerate it.

**Check.** `cargo run -p xtask -- check-refusals` regenerates in memory and diffs byte for byte, then applies:
- (a) Every §8.4 code has a row, and `"{nnn} {plan_text}"` occurs verbatim in that family's §8.4 row (plan lines 765–769). Every active row maps back the same way.
- (b) `exit_code` follows §30.1: 1xx→3, 2xx→3, 3xx→7, 4xx→7, 5xx→8 or 6. The one listed exception is 504→7.
- (c) Every `FMINE-REF-\d{3}` token in `crates/**/*.rs` is a registry code. Tokens in `crates/*/CONTRACT.md` only warn until S3; today 109, 110 and 206 would fail.
- (d) No `fix` contains "clamp" or "re-normalize", case-insensitive.

Proposed rows are reported as warnings. Wire the check into `check_all`. The existing one-way presence check in `fmine-registry` (`src/lib.rs:90-97`) becomes redundant; leave it in place.

**Enum.** `RefusalCode` lands here. `Refusal::new(code: RefusalCode, detail)` is added beside `from_code`. S3 removes `from_code`, its `FMINE-REF-000` fallback (`fmine-evidence/src/lib.rs:26-32`) and the old `REFUSAL_CATALOG`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Parent criterion 1, for active rows: `check-refusals` passes in CI, and plan, registry and catalogue agree on 25 of 25 §8.4 codes. Today 4 of 25 agree.
- Parent criterion 2: running `gen-refusals` twice produces no diff. The committed file's header digest equals `sha256(registries/refusals.toml)`.
- Parent criterion 5: rule (d) passes, and catalogue row 105's "Clamp or re-normalize" is gone.
- `test_load_and_validate_workspace_registries` (`fmine-registry/src/lib.rs:170`) still passes on schema v2.

## Tests and logging
Unit tests in `crates/xtask/src/lib.rs`:
- `test_gen_refusals_golden_three_rows`: a three-row fixture registry produces a byte-exact golden `refusal_catalog.rs`.
- `test_check_refusals_rule_a_plan_text_mismatch_fails` / `_passes`.
- `test_check_refusals_rule_b_family_exit_code_fails`: 201 with exit 4 fails; 504 with exit 7 passes.
- `test_check_refusals_rule_c_unregistered_token_fails`: `FMINE-REF-999` in a `.rs` fixture.
- `test_check_refusals_rule_d_clamp_fix_fails`.
- `test_proposed_rows_warn_not_error`.

**Mutation:**
- `test_mutated_exit_code_detected`: change one registry `exit_code`; the check fails.
- `test_hand_edited_catalogue_detected`: edit one line of the generated file; the diff fails.

**Negative control.** Run `check-refusals` against today's v1 registry (via a schema-v1 adapter, or by hand) and record the counts: 21 of 25 disagree, and 10 rows break the family rule (201–203, 304, 401–404, 501, 504). Quote this in the close reason.

**Log.** One line per code, `{"code","status","plan_ok","exit_ok","fix_ok"}`, and a summary, `{"active":25,"proposed":N,"errors":0,"warnings":N}`.

## Close rule
Close only with this subtask's own evidence, as typed references: `test:<crate>::<path>::<fn>`, `commit:<sha7>`, `record:<path>`, `ci:<run-id>@<sha7>` or an E id. Never a shared or generic reason (K.2 finding 4).

- Parent criterion 2: running `gen-refusals` twice produces no diff. The committed file's header digest equals `sha256(registries/refusals.toml)`.
- Parent criterion 5: rule (d) passes, and catalogue row 105's "Clamp or re-normalize" is gone.
- `test_load_and_validate_workspace_registries` (`fmine-registry/src/lib.rs:170`) still passes on schema v2.

title: BD-328.S3 [WP-06]: Call-site and contract migration
description:
## Context
Subtask S3 of BD-328: "BD-328 [WP-06]: Refusal registry as the single source: plan, registry and compiled catalogue agree; family → exit-code table (§30.1)". The parent bead carries the full background, current state, design, tests and risks; read it first (`br show <parent>`; the parent link is set).

**Parent goal.** - One registry row per code.
- A generated Rust catalogue whose codes form a closed enum, so an unregistered code cannot compile.
- Every call site uses the code whose plan meaning matches the condition.
- Exit codes follow the §30.1 family table.
- A CI check fails on any drift between plan, registry, catalogue and contracts.

## Work
Move every refusal to the code whose plan meaning matches its condition, and delete the unregistered fallback. Depends on S2 (`RefusalCode`, generated catalogue). Proposed codes need S1's decision; until then use the parent's fallback, which is the nearest plan code with a precise `what`, recorded under BD-327's Known gaps.

| `fmine-crs/src/lib.rs:28` CRS mismatch | 101 | 106 |
| `fmine-units/src/lib.rs:33` chemical basis | 107 | 105 |
| `fmine-units/src/lib.rs:32` fraction or moisture outside [0,1] | 105 | 109 |
| `fmine-claim/src/lib.rs:221` Green demanded on placeholder or failed calibration (NL-4) | 401 | 205 |
| `fmine-claim/src/lib.rs:205` missing UU (G-UU) | 404 | 204 |

| `fmine-cli/src/lib.rs:258,263`; `fmine-public/src/lib.rs:804` | 502 | OPEN (S1 point 4) |

- Already correct; leave: fmine-claim 236 (102), 250 (103); fmine-metrics 59 (203); fmine-time 108.
- The loader today emits one refusal for all three lists. Rule (DESIGN): 506 if any file is missing or unreadable; every file is still named.
- The mappers (`refusal_code()`: fmine-crs `lib.rs:24-30`, fmine-time `:28-33`, fmine-units `:28-34`) return `RefusalCode`. The `Display` strings that embed codes (for example `fmine-crs/src/lib.rs:39`) render the code from the enum.

**Delete the fallback** (code only; no file is deleted). Remove:
- `Refusal::from_code` and its `FMINE-REF-000` branch (`fmine-evidence/src/lib.rs:26-32`);
- the hand-written `REFUSAL_CATALOG` (:70-203);

`fmine-cli` (`:5`, `:272`) and `fmine-registry` (`:10`, `:91`) switch to the generated `CATALOG`.

**Contracts.**
- `fmine-claim/CONTRACT.md:22-23` cites 109 and 110 for intensive-add and support mismatch. The plan meanings are 103 and 102.
- `fmine-units/CONTRACT.md:29` cites 206 for an omitted hazardous by-product. No plan code fits, so move it to Known gaps.

After these edits, switch S2's rule (c) to an error for contracts too, and tell BD-327 that its check can do the same.

**Never:**
- map a non-safety condition to a 4xx code;

## Acceptance Criteria

title: NEW [WP-01]: Route public-lane kernels (LMDI, calibration scores, normal CDF/quantile) through `fmine-core::det`; make `xtask check-det` catch method-call transcendentals; cross-ISA golden digest per kernel
description:
## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- plan-deps: none (not in the plan; covers the code part of K.2 finding 5)   proposed-deps: none hard. Blocks the honest rewrite of INT-NUM-001 item 2 (BD-323 subtask 3) only in the sense that the record can list `fmine-metrics::lmdi` and `fmine-calib` as BitwisePortable only after this lands; BD-323 should not wait (write "not yet" now).
- blocks: re-close of BD-010 (the check stops being vacuous); BD-308 claim of BitwisePortable kernels; BD-065/BD-274 public waterfall claims

Type and priority rationale: priority: 1 (§29.2 makes BitwisePortable mandatory for public-lane metrics; the LMDI waterfall and the calibration scores are public-lane outputs and today call the platform libm; INT-NUM-001 claims the opposite in public)

## Background and why it matters
§29.2 says "BitwisePortable: bit-identical across x86_64-linux and aarch64-darwin". It is required for "disclosure-grade outputs: published realization sets, statement numbers, reconciliation certificates, public-lane metrics" (plan line 6619). §29.3 explains why: "`f64::exp`, `ln`, `sin` and `powf` call the platform libm (glibc vs Apple libm)". It gives the rule: "BitwisePortable code calls `fmine-core::det` only. `xtask check-det` flags std transcendentals in modules tagged BitwisePortable."

Round 7 verified that the published record claims more than the code does (R7-C019, VERIFIED). INT-NUM-001 item 2 (`docs/delivery/INT-NUM-001.md:9`) lists fmine-metrics, fmine-calib, -units, -time and -claim as BitwisePortable kernels using `fmine_core::det`. Only fmine-core files declare it, and 15 non-test std transcendental calls sit in calib, numerics and metrics. The checker that should have caught this is vacuous outside fmine-core (K.2 finding 5).

## Goal
- Every production transcendental in fmine-metrics, fmine-calib and fmine-numerics goes through `fmine_core::det`.
- Each of those modules declares `//! Determinism: BitwisePortable`.
- `check-det` would have failed on today's code.
- A cross-ISA golden digest proves equality on the two CI hosts.

## Current state (FACT)
**Std calls in production code** (outside `#[cfg(test)]`):

| File:line | Call |
|---|---|
| `crates/fmine-metrics/src/lmdi.rs:68` | `u.powi(4)`, the series branch of `logarithmic_mean`. Rust documents `powi`'s precision as platform-dependent. |
| `lmdi.rs:70` | `diff / (a.ln() - b.ln())`, two calls |
| `lmdi.rs:101–104, 108, 114` | six `( … ).ln()`, one per factor |
| `crates/fmine-calib/src/lib.rs:211` | `(-0.5*z*z).exp()`, Gaussian CRPS |
| `calib/lib.rs:221` | `(2π).ln()`, a constant, and `sigma.ln()`, the log score |
| `calib/lib.rs:328` | `(-h / range_m).exp()`, the exponential covariance in the Vecchia PIT |
| `crates/fmine-numerics/src/lib.rs:163` | `.exp()` inside `norm_cdf` (Abramowitz & Stegun 7.1.26, documented error < 1.5e-7) |
| `numerics/lib.rs:203, 212` | `.ln()` inside `norm_inv` (Acklam) |

- That is 8 + 4 + 3 = 15, matching R7-C019 (14 if the constant is excluded), plus the one `powi`.
- `.sqrt()` calls are IEEE correctly rounded. They are not a hazard and stay.

**Other relevant facts:**
- **Duplicates.** `fmine-core::det` already has `exp`, `ln`, `powi`, `erf`, `norm_cdf` and `norm_ppf` (Acklam). The numerics versions duplicate them.
  - numerics `norm_inv` silently clamps `p` to `[1e-15, 1-1e-15]` (`numerics/lib.rs:170`).
  - `det::norm_ppf` returns NaN outside [0,1] and ±∞ at the bounds.
  - `norm_inv` has no production caller; only the numerics test at :241 calls it.
  - `norm_cdf` is called by calib at :210 and :382.
- **Dependencies.** All three crates already depend on `fmine-core` (their `Cargo.toml`). No dependency change is needed.
- **The checker.** `xtask check_det_in_source` (`crates/xtask/src/lib.rs:629-643`):
  - runs only on files that contain the literal text "Determinism: BitwisePortable";
  - bans only the call forms `f64::sin(`, `f64::cos(`, `f64::exp(`, `f64::ln(` and `f64::atan2(`. Method calls such as `x.ln()` are never matched;
  - `check_det` skips any file named `det.rs` and reads unreadable files as empty (`unwrap_or_default`, :614).
- **Evidence for det itself.** `test_golden_hash_10k_inputs` (`det.rs:506`) asserts digest `927a7106…1684`, and CI run 40974504857 passed it on ubuntu-latest (x86_64) and macos-14 (aarch64). det has no accuracy tests: only the digest and `test_norm_cdf_and_ppf_roundtrip`.
- **The LMDI test's comment arithmetic is wrong.** The comment at `lmdi.rs:168` says L(2582, 1297) = 1865.629 and a sales-timing effect of −536.71. Computed here (Python, platform libm), they are 1866.348 and −536.915. The test asserts only the range (−550, −500), so it passes.

## Scope
**In:**
- porting the 15 calls and the `powi`;
- delegating numerics `norm_cdf`/`norm_inv` to det;
- module headers;
- the `check-det` rewrite;
- golden digests;
- det accuracy known answers;
- correcting the LMDI comment.

**Out:**
- fmine-crs. It has 14 lines of `sin`/`cos`/`tan`/`powf` but is not claimed BitwisePortable. Its contract should say DeterministicPerIsa (BD-327).
- The silent clamps in calib (`std_dev.max(1e-12)` :208/:219, `alpha.clamp` :227, `epsilon.clamp` :263). These belong to the reopened BD-048 and to BD-328's proposed domain refusal.
- wasm32. Drop the claim from INT-NUM-001; §29.2 does not require it.

## Design
1. **Port.** Each `x.ln()` becomes `det::ln(x)` and each `x.exp()` becomes `det::exp(x)`. `u.powi(4)` becomes `let u2 = u*u; u2*u2`, which is exact IEEE with no libm. `(2π).ln()` becomes a `const LN_2PI: f64` literal; take the value from det at test time and assert it against `det::ln(2.0*PI)`.
2. **Delegate.**
   - `fmine_numerics::norm_cdf(z)` becomes `det::norm_cdf(z)`. This changes calib values at about the 1e-7 level, toward greater accuracy.
   - `norm_inv(p)` becomes `det::norm_ppf(p)`, and the clamp is removed. Out-of-domain input now yields NaN or ±∞, which a caller must refuse. Document this, and add a domain refusal when BD-328 provides a code.
   - Keep both names as thin wrappers, so callers do not churn.
3. **Headers.** Every production `.rs` file in fmine-metrics, fmine-calib and fmine-numerics gets `//! Determinism: <class>`. Lifted files keep line 1 for provenance and put the class on line 2.
4. **The `check-det` rewrite** (about 40 lines):
   - (a) Every production file in a K or E layer crate must carry a `Determinism:` header; a missing header is an error.
   - (b) In BitwisePortable files, ban the regex `\.(ln|log2|log10|ln_1p|exp|exp2|exp_m1|sin|cos|tan|asin|acos|atan|atan2|sinh|cosh|tanh|powf|powi|cbrt|hypot)\(` and the `f64::<same>(` forms.
   - (c) Exempt only `crates/fmine-core/src/det.rs` by full path, not every file named `det.rs`.
   - (d) Unreadable files are errors.
   - Allowed: `sqrt`, `mul_add`, `abs`, `floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `min` and `max`, all correctly rounded or exact (§29.3 FMA row).
5. **Golden digest per kernel.** This follows `det::golden_digest_10k`'s pattern:
   - Generate 10,000 seeded inputs (`fmine-core::rand` Philox, fixed key).
   - Run `logarithmic_mean`, `decompose_aisc_lmdi`, `gaussian_crps`, `log_score` and `norm_cdf`/`norm_inv`.
   - Hash the `to_bits()` outputs with BLAKE3.
   - Assert a committed constant. TARGET: the constant is whatever the first run prints; CI on both ISAs must then agree. A mismatch between hosts is the failure this test exists to catch.
   - Include adversarial ranges: a/b near 1 (the series branch), subnormals, and |z| > 8.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `rg -n '\.(ln|exp|powi|powf|sin|cos|tan)\(' crates/fmine-{metrics,calib,numerics}/src` outside tests returns nothing.
2. Seeded test: `check_det_in_source` on a fixture with `//! Determinism: BitwisePortable` and `x.ln()` fails. Run against today's three crates, the new pattern finds 16 hits (the 15 calls plus the `powi`; counted for this dossier).
3. Five new golden-digest tests pass on ubuntu-latest and macos-14 in one CI run, which is cited by `ci:<id>@<sha>`.
4. Det accuracy known answers pass:
   - `det::ln(2.0) == std::f64::consts::LN_2`;
   - `det::exp(1.0)` within 1 ulp of `E`;
   - `det::norm_cdf(0.0) == 0.5`;
   - `det::norm_ppf(0.5) == 0.0`.
5. The `test_synthetic_two_period_exact_lmdi` residual stays < 1e-11. Its comment states the computed L = 1866.35 and −536.91, or drops the figures.
6. The calib tests stay green, with the ordinal CRPS assertions unchanged.

## Tests
- **Unit:** the known answers above; `check-det` positive and negative fixtures for the method form, the UFCS form, a missing header and an exempted path.
- **Property:**
  - `logarithmic_mean(a, b)` lies between min(a,b) and max(a,b);
  - it is symmetric;
  - it is continuous across the 1e-7 switch, with relative jump < 1e-12 on 10k seeded pairs.
- **Mutation:** re-insert one `.ln()` into `lmdi.rs`; both `check-det` and the LMDI golden digest must fail. The digest fails at least on whichever host's libm differs. INFERENCE: not guaranteed for every input, which is why the lint is the rule.
- **e2e:** `cargo test -p xtask` logs `check-det: N files, 0 violations`.

## Risks, kill criteria and fallbacks
- **det accuracy is unverified beyond the digest.** The lift left frankensim's accuracy tests out (`det.rs:1` "Left out" names only the payne module). If det's `ln` or `exp` errs by more than 1 ulp on the known answers, stop and re-lift the reference tests from `fs-math` at `20463525d`.
- **Performance.** Det functions are slower than libm. LMDI runs per period, not per pixel, so INFERENCE: negligible.
- **Kill:** none. If a kernel cannot be ported, declare it DeterministicPerIsa honestly, and its outputs then cannot be disclosure-grade.
- **Never** assert BitwisePortable in a header or record without the digest test.

## Subtasks
1. **check-det rewrite.** Acceptance: criterion 2. Deps: none.
2. **Port and delegate.** Acceptance: criteria 1, 4, 5 and 6. Deps: none.
3. **Golden digests.** Acceptance: criterion 3. Deps: 2.

## References
- Plan §29.2–29.3 (6612–6630).
- K.2 finding 5. R7-C019 (VERIFIED), R7-C017, R7-C018.

## Work
REVIEW: rule (a), "every production file in a K or E layer crate carries a `Determinism:` header", fails `check-all` on today's code. No K/E file has a header. The workspace's K/E crates (`registries/loc_budget.toml`) are fmine-numerics (K0), fmine-calib (K0), fmine-metrics (E) and fmine-decide (E). fmine-decide is not in the parent's header list. So S1 must add honest headers to the nine files in the same commit, or merge with S2:
- `fmine-numerics/src/{lib,eproc,risk,tropical,voi}.rs`;
- `fmine-calib/src/lib.rs`;
- `fmine-metrics/src/{lib,lmdi}.rs`;
- `fmine-decide/src/lib.rs`.

They all read `//! Determinism: DeterministicPerIsa`, which is true today, since they call platform libm or carry no digest. S2 and S3 change them to BitwisePortable once the digests exist.

**Rewrite `check_det` / `check_det_in_source`** (`crates/xtask/src/lib.rs:600-643`; about 40 lines):
- **(a) Header required.** For crates whose layer (from `check_loc_budget` rows, as `check_claims` does at :543-547) starts with `K` or is `E`, every production `.rs` file must contain `//! Determinism: <Exact|BitwisePortable|DeterministicPerIsa|ThreadVariant>` (§29.2). A missing or unknown class is an error.
- **(b) Banned calls in BitwisePortable files.** After `strip_cfg_test` (:831), strip `//` comments, then ban the method forms `.NAME(` and the `f64::NAME(` forms. NAME is one of: ln, log2, log10, ln_1p, exp, exp2, exp_m1, sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2, sinh, cosh, tanh, powf, powi, cbrt, hypot. xtask has no regex crate, so match the literal strings. Require the `(` immediately after NAME, so that `.exp(` does not match `.exp2(` or `.exp_m1(`. Allowed: `sqrt`, `mul_add`, `abs`, `floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `min` and `max`.
- **(c) Exemption.** Exempt only `crates/fmine-core/src/det.rs`, by its path relative to the root. Today `rs_file.ends_with("det.rs")` (:610) exempts any file of that name.
- **(d) Unreadable files.** An unreadable file is an error. Today `unwrap_or_default` (:614) reads it as empty.
- **Return value.** `check_det` returns the number of files checked, so that `main.rs` can print `check-det: N files, 0 violations`.

Lifted files keep line 1 for provenance (`check_lifts` reads only the first line, :446-448). Insert the class line after the existing licence line.

**Builds on:** nothing. **Hands over:**
- the header slots S2 and S3 flip;

The existing `test_seeded_std_transcendental_in_bitwise_portable_fails` (:871) stays.

title: NEW-det.S2 [WP-01]: Port and delegate
description:
## Context
Subtask S2 of NEW-det: "NEW [WP-01]: Route public-lane kernels (LMDI, calibration scores, normal CDF/quantile) through `fmine-core::det`; make `xtask check-det` catch method-call transcendentals; cross-ISA golden digest per kernel". **Parent goal.** - Every production transcendental in fmine-metrics, fmine-calib and fmine-numerics goes through `fmine_core::det`.
- Each of those modules declares `//! Determinism: BitwisePortable`.
- `check-det` would have failed on today's code.
- A cross-ISA golden digest proves equality on the two CI hosts.

## Work
Port every production std transcendental in fmine-metrics, fmine-calib and fmine-numerics to `fmine_core::det`. Delegate the duplicate normal functions to det, and verify det's own accuracy. All three crates already depend on `fmine-core`, so no `Cargo.toml` changes. This subtask does not depend on S1, but if S1 has landed, its lint guards the result once S3 flips the headers.

**Port** (file:line at 748da79):
- `fmine-metrics/src/lmdi.rs`:
  - :68, `u.powi(4)` → `let u2 = u * u; u2 * u2`;
  - :70, `diff / (a.ln() - b.ln())` → `det::ln`;
  - :101–104, 108 and 114, six `( … ).ln()` → `det::ln(…)`.
- `fmine-calib/src/lib.rs`:
  - :211, `(-0.5*z*z).exp()` → `det::exp`;
  - :221, `(2π).ln()` → `const LN_2PI: f64`, a literal set to the value `det::ln(2.0 * PI)` returns; the test asserts bit equality;
  - :221, `sigma.ln()` → `det::ln`;
  - :328, `(-h / self.range_m).exp()` → `det::exp`.
- `fmine-numerics/src/lib.rs`:
  - `norm_cdf` (:154) becomes a thin wrapper over `det::norm_cdf`. This removes the A&S 7.1.26 body and its `.exp()` at :163. Calib values change at about the 1e-7 level, toward greater accuracy.
  - `norm_inv` (:169) becomes a wrapper over `det::norm_ppf`. Delete the silent clamp at :170 (`p.clamp(1e-15, 1.0 - 1e-15)`). Out-of-domain p now yields NaN, or ±∞ at 0 and 1 (`det.rs:291-300`). Document that callers must refuse such values. The only caller is the numerics test at :241; calib calls only `norm_cdf` (:210, :382).

Keep both wrapper names, so callers do not churn. `.sqrt()` stays: it is correctly rounded.

**Comment fix** (`lmdi.rs:168`). It says L(2582, 1297) = 1865.629 and −536.71. The parent computes 1866.348 and −536.915, and this enrichment's re-run gives 1866.348 and −536.915. Write "L ≈ 1866.35, effect ≈ −536.91", or drop the figures. The assertion range (−550, −500) stays.

**Out of scope; do not touch:**
- calib's silent clamps (`std_dev.max(1e-12)` :208/:219, `alpha.clamp` :227, `epsilon.clamp` :263), which belong to BD-048 and BD-328;
- fmine-crs trigonometry (DeterministicPerIsa; BD-327);
- the clamp in `fmine-metrics/src/lib.rs:188` (`recovery_fn(g).clamp(0.05, 0.999)` in `solve_cutoff_grade`). Report it to BD-328/BD-275 instead.

**Hands over.** Ported kernels to S3, which adds the digests and changes lmdi.rs, calib lib.rs and numerics lib.rs to `BitwisePortable`. Per the parent, BitwisePortable is never asserted without the digest test.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Parent criterion 1: `rg -n '\.(ln|exp|powi|powf|sin|cos|tan)\(' crates/fmine-{metrics,calib,numerics}/src`, ignoring `#[cfg(test)]` modules, returns nothing. `fmine-metrics/src/lib.rs:271` is inside the test module (which starts at :198) and does not count.
- Parent criterion 4, as tests in `fmine-core/src/det.rs`:
  - `det::ln(2.0) == std::f64::consts::LN_2`;
  - `det::exp(1.0)` within 1 ulp of `E`;
  - `det::norm_cdf(0.0) == 0.5`;
  - `det::norm_ppf(0.5) == 0.0`.

  If `ln` or `exp` misses by more than 1 ulp, stop and re-lift fs-math's reference tests at `20463525d` (parent Risks).
- Parent criterion 5: `test_synthetic_two_period_exact_lmdi` (`lmdi.rs:134`) still has a residual below 1e-11, and its comment is corrected.
- Parent criterion 6: the calib tests (:402, :423, :437, :464) stay green with the ordinal CRPS assertions unchanged.

## Tests and logging
- `test_det_ln_2_equals_ln_2_constant`, `test_det_exp_1_within_one_ulp`, `test_det_norm_cdf_zero_is_half`, `test_det_norm_ppf_half_is_zero` (fmine-core).
- `test_ln_2pi_literal_matches_det` (fmine-calib).
- `test_norm_inv_out_of_domain_is_nan_not_clamped`: p = −0.1 and p = 1.1 give NaN; p = 0 gives −∞.
- Property tests on 10k seeded pairs (Philox, fixed `RngKey`):
  - `test_logarithmic_mean_between_min_and_max`;
  - `test_logarithmic_mean_symmetric`;
  - `test_logarithmic_mean_continuous_at_series_switch`: relative jump below 1e-12 across the 1e-7 switch at `lmdi.rs:66`.

**Mutation** (run in S3's commit, once lmdi.rs declares BitwisePortable). Re-insert `a.ln()` at `lmdi.rs:70`. S1's lint must flag it, and S3's LMDI digest must fail on at least one host. INFERENCE: the digest is not guaranteed to catch every input, which is why the lint is the rule. Before the header flips, S1's rule (b) does not scan the file. Until then the guard is criterion 1's grep.

**Log.** The property tests print `{"test","cases":10000,"key":"<hex>","max_rel_jump"}`.

Close only with this subtask's own evidence, as typed references: `test:<crate>::<path>::<fn>`, `commit:<sha7>`, `record:<path>`, `ci:<run-id>@<sha7>` or an E id. Never a shared or generic reason (K.2 finding 4).

title: NEW-det.S3 [WP-01]: Golden digests
description:
## Context
Subtask S3 of NEW-det: "NEW [WP-01]: Route public-lane kernels (LMDI, calibration scores, normal CDF/quantile) through `fmine-core::det`; make `xtask check-det` catch method-call transcendentals; cross-ISA golden digest per kernel". The parent bead carries the full background, current state, design, tests and risks; read it first (`br show <parent>`; the parent link is set).

**Parent goal.** - Every production transcendental in fmine-metrics, fmine-calib and fmine-numerics goes through `fmine_core::det`.
- Each of those modules declares `//! Determinism: BitwisePortable`.
- `check-det` would have failed on today's code.
- A cross-ISA golden digest proves equality on the two CI hosts.

## Work
Prove cross-ISA bit equality for the ported public-lane kernels with one golden digest per kernel, then declare their modules BitwisePortable. Depends on S2; if S1 has landed, its lint then guards the flipped files.

**Pattern.** Follow `fmine_core::det::golden_digest_10k` (`crates/fmine-core/src/det.rs:487-500`):
- generate 10,000 deterministic inputs;
- evaluate the kernel;
- append each output's `to_bits().to_le_bytes()`;
- BLAKE3 the bytes with `fmine_core::hash::blake3_hash` (`hash.rs:356`);
- compare the hex with a committed constant.

Inputs come from `fmine_core::rand::PhiloxStream::new(RngKey { … })` (`rand.rs:87`) with a fixed key written in the test. Use `next_f64_open01` (:116) and scale from there.

**Five digest functions and tests** (DESIGN names; one per kernel the parent lists):
1. `logarithmic_mean` (`fmine-metrics/src/lmdi.rs:63`). Include pairs with |a−b|/mean below 1e-7, on the series branch at :66; pairs at large ratios; and subnormal-adjacent magnitudes.
2. `decompose_aisc_lmdi` (`lmdi.rs:75`), over seeded strictly positive `LmdiState` pairs. Hash all six effects and `total_delta`.
3. `gaussian_crps` (`fmine-calib/src/lib.rs:207`). Include |z| > 8.
4. `gaussian_log_score` (`calib/lib.rs:218`). The parent calls it `log_score`; the real name is `gaussian_log_score`.
5. `norm_cdf` and `norm_inv` (`fmine-numerics/src/lib.rs:154`, `:169`), now det wrappers. Include |z| > 8, and p near 0 and 1.

Each kernel crate gets `pub fn golden_digest_<kernel>_10k() -> String` beside the kernel, and a test asserting the constant.

The constants are TARGETs: each is whatever the first run prints. Commit it, then require ubuntu-latest (x86_64) and macos-14 (aarch64) to agree in one CI run. A mismatch between hosts is exactly the failure the test exists to catch. Never "fix" it by regenerating the constant on the second host.

**Header flips** after the digests pass on both hosts:
- `lmdi.rs`, `fmine-calib/src/lib.rs` and `fmine-numerics/src/lib.rs` become `//! Determinism: BitwisePortable`.
- `fmine-numerics/src/lib.rs` also holds `cholesky_solve` and `brent_root`. A per-file class must cover them, so either add both to digest 5's byte stream or leave the file DeterministicPerIsa. OPEN; the implementer records the choice.
- `fmine-metrics/src/lib.rs`, the lifted numerics files and `fmine-decide` stay DeterministicPerIsa: no digest covers them.

**Hands over** (FACT targets for other beads):
- BD-323.S3's INT-NUM-001 line 9 can now list these modules as BitwisePortable, citing this subtask's `ci:<id>@<sha>`;
- BD-010 gains a non-vacuous check;
- BD-065 and BD-274 may cite the LMDI digest.

wasm32 stays untested and unclaimed (§29.2 does not require it).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Parent criterion 3: five new golden-digest tests pass on ubuntu-latest and macos-14 in the same CI run. Cite it as `ci:<run>@<sha7>`.
- `check-det` passes with the three flipped files declaring BitwisePortable. S1's lint then reports 0 violations in them.
- Every BitwisePortable header in the three crates corresponds to a digest test in the same crate. A one-off grep pairs them, and the close reason quotes it.
- No constant is regenerated after the first host commits it. `git log -p` on the test file shows a single value per digest.

## Tests and logging
Tests next to each kernel:
- `test_golden_digest_logarithmic_mean_10k`;
- `test_golden_digest_decompose_aisc_lmdi_10k`;
- `test_golden_digest_gaussian_crps_10k`;
- `test_golden_digest_gaussian_log_score_10k`;
- `test_golden_digest_norm_cdf_inv_10k`.

Also `test_digest_inputs_cover_series_branch_and_tails`, which asserts that the generator emits at least one series-branch pair and at least one |z| > 8.

**Mutation.**
- Swap `det::ln` for `f64::ln` in a scratch copy of lmdi.rs. The lint must fail, and the LMDI digest is expected to fail on at least one host. INFERENCE: not guaranteed for every input set.
- Change one Philox key word. Every digest must change.

**Log.** Each digest test prints `{"kernel","n":10000,"rng_key":"<hex>","digest":"<blake3 hex>","target":"<triple>"}`. The CI summary line lists the five digests per host. The close reason quotes both hosts' lines.

## Close rule
Close only with this subtask's own evidence, as typed references: `test:<crate>::<path>::<fn>`, `commit:<sha7>`, `record:<path>`, `ci:<run-id>@<sha7>` or an E id. Never a shared or generic reason (K.2 finding 4).

- Every BitwisePortable header in the three crates corresponds to a digest test in the same crate. A one-off grep pairs them, and the close reason quotes it.
- No constant is regenerated after the first host commits it. `git log -p` on the test file shows a single value per digest.

title: fmine-io: shell-to-design loss: an OMF design pit against a certified shell, exact enclosures
description:
Plan §15.5 (Pit and ramp design): FrankenMining ingests the engineer's designed pit and computes the shell-to-design loss (tonnes, metal, value). The parts exist but are not wired: OMF Surface -> certified closed mesh and per-block proportions (bd-aqfl, bd-wn57, fmine_geom::volcert) and the certified ultimate pit / nested shells on the same block model (bd-joiv).

Scope (fmine-io omf::pit):
- PitModel::design(surface, depth): each parent block's certified proportion inside the closed design surface, in pitflow order, as sub-cell counts [inside, inside+band] of 8^depth. Refuse a design whose bounding box leaves the block model (no blocks to value there).
- Design::total(weights): exact enclosure of the design's total of any per-block quantity (value, tonnes, metal).
- Design::against(shell, weights): shell total, design total, the shell's part left outside the design, the design's part added outside the shell, and the loss (shell - design = left - added), each an exact integer enclosure in sub-cells.

Acceptance: unit test on the 15-block section with a design box: at sub-cell-aligned faces every enclosure is exact and equals the hand values (pit 5, design -7, left -4, added -16, loss 12 quarter-units; tonnes); an off-grid design's enclosure contains the hand value; the identity loss = left - added = shell - design holds; refusals (not a Surface, missing, outside the model, wrong lengths, depth). Planted bug caught. CONTRACT fmine-io updated.

No-claim: geometric enclosure only, no grade uncertainty (no geostats); quantities spread evenly in each block; the design is not checked against slopes; no ramp-flattening; one hand model; no CLI verb.
close_reason: commit:cf55590 test:crates/fmine-io/src/omf/tests.rs#a_designed_pit_against_the_certified_shell_gives_its_loss_in_exact_enclosures; planted layer-order bug caught; fresh re-run at HEAD; not independently verified

comments.author: SwiftBasin
comments.text:
Delivered in commit:cf55590 (local main, not pushed).

**What it does** (plan §15.5 shell-to-design loss). This joins finished pieces: OMF Surface → certified closed mesh → `volcert::block_proportions`, and the certified pit and shells on the same block model.
- `PitModel::design(surface, depth)`: each parent block's certified proportion inside the closed design, as sub-cells [inside, inside+band] of 8^depth, in pitflow order. A design whose bounding box leaves the model's blocks is refused.
- `Design::against(shell, weights)` works for any shell flags and any integer per-block quantity (value, tonnes, metal). It gives shell, design, left (shell outside the design), added (design outside the shell), and loss = shell − design = left − added. Each is an exact integer enclosure. `Design::total` gives the design's total alone, and `Design::cells` gives one block's sub-cells.

**Acceptance**
1. test:crates/fmine-io/src/omf/tests.rs#a_designed_pit_against_the_certified_shell_gives_its_loss_in_exact_enclosures
   - The box at sub-cell faces is exact at depth 1. Pit 5, design −7, left −4, added −16, loss 12 quarter-units. Tonnes: 14.4 t against 10.8 t.
   - The deep design (top layer left out) is worth 9, so its loss is −4. The slopes are not checked, as documented.
   - The rough design (sides 0.25 m and 0.5 m off the faces) encloses the hand −7.48 at depths 1–4: [−19,−7], [−13,−7], [−10,−7], [−8.5,−7], each half as wide. loss == shell − design as an interval at every depth.
   - Six refusals: outside the model; missing; not a Surface; depth 99; short shell; short weights.
2. Planted: the proportions left in OMF layer order. The deep design failed, while the full-height boxes, the same in every layer, passed. Reverted.
3. CONTRACT fmine-io §2, §4, §5, §6 (PO-IO-13) and §10.

**Gates before commit:**
- fmt and clippy `-D warnings` on fmine-io all-targets (ovh-b) passed.

- check-all exited 0 (check-det 36, gate-oracle-01 8).

title: BD-326 [WP-00]: `deny.toml` in CI with the rider-licence allow-list and duplicate policy; `franken-stack.lock` row ids aligned with F.2
description:
_Plan row BD-326 (WP-00). Scope in one line: `cargo deny` in CI with the rider-licence and duplicate policy; `franken-stack.lock` row ids aligned with Appendix F (FD-…-00) and `fastmcp-rust` named_

## Dependencies as researched (2026-10-29, HEAD 748da79)
- Plan row's blocked-by list: BD-005
- plan-deps: BD-005   proposed-deps: none hard. BD-005 is closed but its done-when is unmet (R7-C015). This bead does not need BD-005's transitive walker (cargo-deny walks the graph itself). Land the FD-id rename together with, or before, BD-323's record rewrite, since both edit `docs/delivery/INT-*.md` and `docs/adr/ADR-RNG-01.md`.
- blocks: WP-04's first bead that adds asupersync; INT-AS-001a PASS (BD-325)

Type and priority rationale: priority: 2 (the build graph holds no external crate today, so deny cannot fail on licences or duplicates yet; it becomes the gate the moment WP-04 adds asupersync, and the lock-id collision already mislabels three committed records)

## Background and why it matters
Rule L-5 (§28.5) and §31.5 make `deny.toml` and the banned list CI gates, and ask for a closed dependency universe with a reason per crate. Round 7 found two problems with the committed config (K.2 finding 8):
- It is not run in CI.
- If it were run against the suite's real foundation, it would fail for the wrong reasons (R7-C150). The auditors ran cargo-deny 0.20.2 on a scratch crate that depends on asupersync `=0.5.0` (default features off) and got:
  - four `LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider` rejections (asupersync, franken-decision, franken-evidence, franken-kernel);
  - nine duplicate-version errors (block-buffer, const-oid, cpufeatures, crypto-common, digest, getrandom, rand_core, sha2, syn);
  - `tokio` reached through `wasm-bindgen-futures`, because no `[graph] targets` is set;
  - with the `tls` feature, `time` 0.3.55 via x509-parser/asn1-rs/der-parser.

  The plan's L-5 allows `time`/`chrono` transitively on exactly those foundation paths, but `deny.toml` bans them outright.

Separately, `franken-stack.lock` names its rows `FD-…-01`. Appendix F.1 makes `FD-…-00` canonical, and F.2 already uses `-01` for upstream asks. Nine of the fourteen lock ids therefore name a different object in the plan (R7-C162). The lock also names crates.io `fastmcp`, an unrelated project whose only version is 0.0.0. The suite's package is `fastmcp-rust` (R7-C163).

## Goal
- CI runs `cargo deny check` on every push, and passes today.
- The config already expresses the rider-licence decision, the duplicate policy and the L-5 transitive allow-paths, so the WP-04 asupersync entry needs only row additions, not a redesign.
- Every lock row id is `FD-<X>-00` and matches an Appendix F.1 row.
- A check keeps the lock and F.1 aligned.

## Current state (FACT)
- **`deny.toml`:**
  - `[advisories] yanked = "deny"`;
  - `[licenses] allow = [MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, Unicode-3.0, Zlib]`, with no `exceptions` and no `clarify`;
  - `[bans] multiple-versions = "deny"`, `wildcards = "deny"`;
  - 22 denied names, including `time` and `chrono` outright;
  - no `petgraph`, `fastembed` or `tantivy`, although L-5 bans them;
  - no `[graph]` section.
- **CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): `xtask check-all`, `cargo check`, `cargo test`, on ubuntu-latest and macos-14 × dev/release. There is no deny, clippy or fmt step. Run 40974504857 is green.
- **Graph:** `Cargo.lock` holds 16 workspace packages and no external crate.
- **Licences:**
  - The workspace declares `license = "MIT"` (`Cargo.toml:26`), while `LICENSE` reads "MIT License (with OpenAI/Anthropic Rider)" (E681). frankensim's LICENSE is the same text. asupersync's manifest declares `license = "LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider"`.
  - Whether the rider is acceptable in a client-facing product is RISK-17 / OPEN-STRATA-6 (owner and counsel, before M2).
- **`franken-stack.lock`:** 14 rows, FD-AS-01 … FD-FTUI-01; `name = "fastmcp"` at line 127. F.1 has 15 FD-…-00 rows; the lock has no FD-FMD-00 row (franken_markdown, frankenmermaid).
- **Ids collide with F.2 asks:** FD-AS-01, FD-FSIM-01, FD-FA-01, FD-FSCI-01, FD-FP-01, FD-FNP-01, FD-FJ-01, FD-FSYM-01, FD-FGDB-01.
- **Committed citations of `-01` ids:**
  - `docs/delivery/INT-AS-001.md:5`;
  - `docs/delivery/INT-NUM-001.md:5`;
  - `docs/adr/ADR-RNG-01.md:8`.

## Scope
**In:**
- `deny.toml` rewrite;
- CI job;
- lock rename and the `fastmcp-rust` fix;
- the FD-FMD-00 row;
- the three citation edits;
- a lock ↔ F.1 id check.

**Out:**
- one-package-id and criterion 9 (BD-325);
- choosing whether the rider is acceptable (owner and counsel, RISK-17). This bead records the owner's decision; it does not make it.

## Design
**`deny.toml` (target shape):**
- `[graph] targets = ["x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", "aarch64-apple-darwin", "wasm32-unknown-unknown"]`. wasm32 is in `rust-toolchain.toml`; keep it, and handle tokio with a wrapper.
- `[licenses]` keeps the allow list. Rider crates are admitted only by named `[[licenses.exceptions]]` entries, each with a comment citing the owner's RISK-17 record:
  - for the workspace's own crates: `fmine-*`, `xtask`;
  - for the suite crates when they enter: asupersync, asupersync-macros, franken-decision, franken-evidence, franken-kernel, ftui.

  License-file siblings get `[[licenses.clarify]]` entries with the LICENSE hash. Do not add `LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider` to the global allow list.
- **Workspace licence field (DESIGN, owner decision).** The own crates should declare what the LICENSE says, either `license = "LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider"` (asupersync's form) or `license-file = "LICENSE"` (frankensim's form). Until the owner decides, keep "MIT" and record the discrepancy in the deny file comment.
- `[bans]`:
  - keep `multiple-versions = "deny"`, with an empty `skip` list now. When asupersync enters, add the nine pairs, each with a reason; FA's deny.toml at `41363acb` skips the same pairs (R7-C150).
  - `wildcards = "deny"` with `allow-wildcard-paths = true`, plus `publish = false` on every workspace crate. HYPOTHESIS: today's path dependencies have no version, so they count as wildcards and would fail without this. Verify on the first CI run.
  - Add `petgraph`, `fastembed` and `tantivy` to `deny`.
  - Replace the outright `time`/`chrono` bans with `{ name = "time", wrappers = ["x509-parser", "asn1-rs", "der-parser", "fsqlite-func", "fastmcp-server", "fp-types"] }`, and the same for chrono. cargo-deny matches wrappers against immediate parents only (R7-C152).
  - Add `{ name = "tokio", wrappers = ["wasm-bindgen-futures"] }` only if the probe shows it; otherwise keep tokio fully banned.
- `[advisories]`: `yanked = "deny"`, default database.

**CI job** (one extra job, Linux only, since the licence and bans result does not depend on the host): `taiki-e/install-action` with `tool: cargo-deny`, pinned to a version, then `cargo deny --locked check advisories bans licenses sources`. Use `[sources] allow-git` limited to the suite's GitHub org. Advisories need network access; if the advisory database fetch flakes, retry once and do not mark the step optional.

**Lock alignment:**
- Rename the 14 ids to `-00`.
- Row FD-FMCP-00 gets `name = "fastmcp-rust"` with a comment ("crates.io `fastmcp` is an unrelated project, R7-C163").
- Add FD-FMD-00 (franken_markdown + frankenmermaid, consume in `fmine-report` only, fallback "plain markdown without diagrams").
- Fix the three citations.

**Lock ↔ F.1 check** (about 40 lines in xtask): parse `id = "FD-…"` from the lock and `| FD-[A-Z]+-00 |` rows from the plan's Appendix F.1 table. The two sets must be equal, and no lock id may match `-0[1-9]`. Reading the plan from xtask is acceptable here, because F.1 is the canonical id source by the plan's own text.

**Worked example.** Today `cargo deny check` sees 16 workspace crates with licence "MIT" (allowed). The expected result is PASS, given the wildcard setting above. Two seeded checks run as local negative controls and are recorded in the close reason, not added to CI:
1. A scratch member that adds `tokio = "1"` fails `bans`.
2. The R7 probe crate on asupersync `=0.5.0` fails `licenses` until the exceptions block is uncommented, and fails `bans` with nine duplicates until the skip block is added.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. CI runs `cargo deny check` (all four checks) on every push, and the job is green on the bead's commit.
2. `franken-stack.lock` ids are all `FD-*-00`, equal to the F.1 set (15 rows including FD-FMD-00). `xtask` fails on a seeded `-01` id.
3. `grep -rn "FD-[A-Z]*-01" docs/ franken-stack.lock` returns nothing.
4. `deny.toml` bans petgraph, fastembed and tantivy, and uses wrappers for time and chrono.
5. The close reason quotes the two negative controls' outputs.

## Tests
- **xtask unit tests for the id check:** `-01` rejected; a missing FD-FMD-00 rejected; an extra lock row not in F.1 rejected.
- **CI job:** `cargo deny check` itself.
- **Negative controls:** the two local probes above, with output quoted. Keep the probe crate outside the repository, or in a scratch directory that is never committed.

## Risks, kill criteria and fallbacks
- **The rider exception without counsel.** Write the exceptions now, but label them "pending RISK-17". If counsel rejects the rider for client-facing builds, the plan's own fallback is "lift only into internal builds; no client distribution" (§36.2, line 7475).
- **Advisory database network failures in CI:** retry; never `continue-on-error`.
- **Wildcard behaviour is uncertain (HYPOTHESIS above).** If `allow-wildcard-paths` does not clear it, add `version = "0.1.0"` to the path dependencies instead.
- **Never:** add the rider licence to the global allow list; weaken `multiple-versions` to "warn".

## Subtasks
1. **Lock and citation alignment.** Rename the ids, fix the `fastmcp-rust` name, add FD-FMD-00, edit the three docs, and add the xtask id check. Acceptance: criteria 2 and 3. Deps: none.
2. **`deny.toml` and the CI job.** Use the target shape above. Run the probes locally. Acceptance: criteria 1, 4 and 5. Deps: none.

## References
- Plan §27.5 (fastmcp row, line 6345), §28.5 L-5 (6563–6577), §31.5 (7041–7050), RISK-17 (7439), Appendix F.1/F.2 (8696–8762), BD-326 row (7906), K.2 finding 8.
- R7-C150, R7-C151, R7-C152, R7-C162, R7-C163. E681, E683.
- Files: `deny.toml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `franken-stack.lock`, `Cargo.toml`, `LICENSE`, `~/projects/asupersync/Cargo.toml` (licence field), `docs/delivery/INT-*.md`, `docs/adr/ADR-RNG-01.md`.

## E2E test script and logging
- **E2E.** The CI job, plus one local run of `cargo deny check` and `cargo xtask check-stack-lock` with their output quoted. Both negative controls (an unlisted licence and a duplicate version) must fail with the offending crate named.
- **Logging.** The `check-stack-lock` xtask prints one line per F.1 row (`id`, `crate`, `pinned`, `status`) and one per extra or missing row. No harness beyond that (no-bloat rule).

2. `franken-stack.lock` ids are all `FD-*-00`, equal to the F.1 set (15 rows including FD-FMD-00). `xtask` fails on a seeded `-01` id.
3. `grep -rn "FD-[A-Z]*-01" docs/ franken-stack.lock` returns nothing.
4. `deny.toml` bans petgraph, fastembed and tantivy, and uses wrappers for time and chrono.
5. The close reason quotes the two negative controls' outputs.

available, or otherwise permit access to the Software … to or for any Restricted Party"; "use" includes
incorporation into ML or automated pipelines.
- In short: no rights to OpenAI, Anthropic, their affiliates or anyone acting on their behalf.
The row now names the agent-access question (agents hosted by those parties reading through `fmine-mcp` or the CLI,
§30.4) and adds the deadline "before the M2 agent slice opens" (new bead bd-onu6). The decision this bead records
should answer that question explicitly. Not edited: the §36 row for RISK-17 / OPEN-STRATA-6 (line 7483) still has
the fallback "Lift only into internal builds; no client distribution", which cannot apply when the product itself
carries the rider; flagged for the owner.

description:
## Context

F.1 says "pinned library; default features" and gives no exact pin, so write `pin = "OPEN"` with a comment. Do not invent a version.

**Citations.** These are the same three edits as BD-323.S3 (`bd-oukb.3`). Whichever subtask lands first makes them:
- `docs/delivery/INT-AS-001.md:5` (FD-AS-00);
- `docs/delivery/INT-NUM-001.md:5` (four ids);

- It delegates to a pure `pub fn compare_lock_to_f1(lock: &str, plan: &str) -> Result<(), Vec<String>>`, which:

  - collects `| FD-[A-Z]+-00 |` row ids only between the `### F.1` and `### F.2` headings. F.2 rows legitimately start `| FD-FA-01 |`.
  - fails if the two sets differ, naming each missing or extra id;
  - fails on any lock id matching `-0[1-9]$`;
  - fails if either set is empty, so that a moved heading is not silently accepted.
- Register it in `crates/xtask/src/main.rs` as `check-stack-lock`, and call it from `check_all` (:645).

xtask has no dependencies (`crates/xtask/Cargo.toml`), so parse with `strip_kv_str` (:687) and plain string scanning.

**Scope limit.** Do not make the check ban `FD-*-01` in `docs/` permanently. F.2's upstream-ask ids (FD-FA-01 … FD-FA-16) are valid citations in future docs. Parent criterion 3 is a one-off grep at this commit.

title: BD-326.S2 [WP-00]: `deny.toml` and the CI job
description:
## Context
Subtask S2 of BD-326: "BD-326 [WP-00]: `deny.toml` in CI with the rider-licence allow-list and duplicate policy; `franken-stack.lock` row ids aligned with F.2". - A check keeps the lock and F.1 aligned.

## Work
Rewrite `deny.toml` to the parent's target shape, run it in CI on every push, and record two local negative controls. Today `deny.toml` (44 lines) has no `[graph]`, no licence exceptions, bans `time` and `chrono` outright (lines 42–43), and lacks `petgraph`, `fastembed` and `tantivy`. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, one matrix job) has no deny step.

**`deny.toml`:**
- **`[graph]`.** `targets = ["x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", "aarch64-apple-darwin", "wasm32-unknown-unknown"]`. wasm32 is in `rust-toolchain.toml:7`.
- **`[advisories]`.** `yanked = "deny"`, default database.
- **`[licenses]`.**
  - Keep the allow list exactly. Never add `LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider` to it.
  - Add `[[licenses.exceptions]]` blocks for the rider crates: the own crates `fmine-*` and `xtask`, and the suite crates asupersync, asupersync-macros, franken-decision, franken-evidence, franken-kernel and ftui. Each block carries the comment "pending RISK-17 owner/counsel decision".
  - Suite crates are not in the graph, so their blocks are commented out until WP-04. The `[[licenses.clarify]]` entries for LICENSE files arrive with those crates.
  - Workspace `license = "MIT"` (`Cargo.toml:26`) disagrees with `LICENSE` ("MIT License (with OpenAI/Anthropic Rider)", E681). Record the disagreement in a comment and leave the field to the owner.
- **`[bans]`.**
  - `multiple-versions = "deny"`, with an empty `skip`. Add a commented block holding the nine R7-C150 pairs: block-buffer, const-oid, cpufeatures, crypto-common, digest, getrandom, rand_core, sha2 and syn.
  - `wildcards = "deny"` with `allow-wildcard-paths = true`. Add `publish = false` to every workspace `Cargo.toml` (xtask already has it).
  - Add `petgraph`, `fastembed` and `tantivy` to `deny`.
  - Replace the outright bans with `{ name = "time", wrappers = ["x509-parser", "asn1-rs", "der-parser", "fsqlite-func", "fastmcp-server", "fp-types"] }`, and the same for `chrono`. cargo-deny matches immediate parents only (R7-C152).
  - Keep `tokio` fully banned unless the probe shows the `wasm-bindgen-futures` path.
- **`[sources]`.** `unknown-git = "deny"`; allow git only from the suite's GitHub org (`Cargo.toml:28`).

**CI.** Add a separate Linux-only job:
- `taiki-e/install-action` with `tool: cargo-deny@0.20.2`, the version R7 used (R7-C150);
- then `cargo deny --locked check advisories bans licenses sources`;
- on an advisory-database fetch failure, retry once;
- never use `continue-on-error`.

**Negative controls.** Run them locally, with the probe crates outside the repository (in the scratchpad). Quote their outputs in the close reason. Commit neither.
1. A scratch member with `tokio = "1"` fails `bans`.
2. The R7 probe on asupersync `=0.5.0` (default features off):
   - fails `licenses` with the four rider rejections until the exceptions block is uncommented;
   - fails `bans` with the nine duplicates until the skip block is added.

**Never** weaken `multiple-versions` to "warn", or allow the rider globally.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Parent criterion 1: the deny job runs on every push and pull request, and is green on this subtask's commit. Cite it as `ci:<run>@<sha7>`.
- Parent criterion 4:
  - `deny.toml` bans petgraph, fastembed and tantivy;

- The wildcard HYPOTHESIS is settled on the first CI run. If `allow-wildcard-paths` does not clear the path dependencies, add `version = "0.1.0"` to them instead (parent fallback), and state which fix was used.

- **Log.** Run with `--format json`. Record one line per check, `{"check":"bans|licenses|advisories|sources","status","errors","warnings"}`, and one summary line, `{"deny_version":"0.20.2","targets":3,"result"}`.
